2601.09351.tldr: This chapter explores how AI-empowered industrial innovation inherently intersects with ethics, as advancements in AI introduce new challenges related to transparency, accountability, and fairness.

2601.09353.tldr: This work considers a Monte-Carlo Tree Search planning approach for single-agent autonomous driving in lane-free traffic, where the associated Markov Decision Process the authors formulate is influenced from existing approaches tied to reinforcement learning frameworks.

2601.09365.tldr: This work evaluates a model's ability to establish common ground by utilizing "relational references" in the dynamic and shared environments of situated dialogs and proposes approaches to improve their performance by using reinforcement learning on synthetically generated dialog data.

2601.09381.tldr: Two logics for weighted finite structures: first-order logic with summation (FO(SUM)) and its recursive extension IFP(SUM) are discussed and fundamental results on their expressiveness and computational complexity are discussed.

2601.09382.tldr: This paper proposes a novel interaction paradigm for proactive Task-oriented Agents capable of bridging the gap between relatively static user's needs and a dynamic environment, and introduces a high-quality data synthesis pipeline to construct complex, multi-turn dialog data in a dynamic environment.

2601.09398.tldr: ACT (Activation-Guided Channel-wise Ability Transfer), which localizes ability-relevant channels via activation differences and selectively transfers only the corresponding parameters, followed by lightweight fine-tuning for compatibility, can recover forgotten abilities while preserving retained skills.

2601.09413.tldr: A voice-agentic framework that learns one critical omni-understanding skill: knowing when to trust itself versus when to consult external audio perception, and generalizes naturally from speech recognition to complex, multiple-choice audio reasoning.

2601.09416.tldr: The use of radiomic features as additional input in model training effectively improved the classification performance, in addition to its added benefits in interpretability, and a hierarchical loss is proposed to optimize two binary classification tasks with hierarchical classes.

2601.09433.tldr: This paper is the first to apply the recently proposed Vision Transformer (ViT) deep learning architecture to the task of identification of semantic elements on coins, using fully automatic learning from multi-modal data (images and unstructured text).

2601.09445.tldr: This work designs a framework based on mechanistic interpretability methods to identify where and how conflicting knowledge from the pre-training data is encoded within LMs, and demonstrates how mechanistic interpretability methods can be leveraged to causally intervene in and control conflicting knowledge at inference time.

2601.09446.tldr: The comprehensive fine-tuning, incremental inference, and verification modules reduce error rates, increase predicate coverage, and improve reasoning performance for smaller LMs, moving us closer to developing reliable and accessible symbolic-reasoning systems.

2601.09448.tldr: A Large Language Model (LLM)-based alternative that maps natural language text prompts to equalization settings enables a conversational approach to sound system control and indicates that LLMs could function as artificial equalizers, contributing to the development of more accessible, context-aware, and expert-level audio tuning methods.

2601.09451.tldr: Results show that Quamba- SE consistently outperforms Quamba, achieving up to +2.68% on individual benchmarks and up to +0.83% improvement in the average accuracy of 6 datasets.

2601.09455.tldr: An overview of the computational complexity results in the literature for generating explanations is provided, finding that in many cases, generating explanations is computationally hard.

2601.09460.tldr: A unified framework is introduced that generalizes common phases across CPCL paradigms, and secure noise sampling is identified as the foundational phase to achieve CPCL, and trade-offs of different secure noise sampling techniques, noise types, and DP mechanisms are analyzed.

2601.09467.tldr: The Searth Transformer is proposed, a physics-informed architecture that incorporates zonal periodicity and meridional boundaries into window-based self-attention for physically consistent global information exchange and a Relay Autoregressive (RAR) fine-tuning strategy that enables learning long-range atmospheric evolution under constrained memory and computational budgets.

2601.09503.tldr: This work proposes Task-to-Quiz (T2Q), a deterministic and automated evaluation paradigm designed to decouple task execution from world-state understanding, and identifies proactive exploration and fine-grained state representation as primary bottlenecks.

2601.09518.tldr: D-STAR (Decoupled Spatio-Temporal Action Reasoner), a hierarchical policy that disentangles when to act from where to act, is introduced, a complete, effective pipeline for learning complex whole-body interactions from HHI data.

2601.09520.tldr: A semi-supervised method to automatically curate a large and diverse corpus of one-shot drum samples from unlabeled audio sources, which is used to synthesize a high-quality dataset from MIDI files alone, which is used to train a sequence-to-sequence transcription model.

2601.09527.tldr: The results show that consumer GPUs can reliably replace cloud inference for most SME workloads, except latency-critical long-context RAG, where high-end GPUs remain essential.

2601.09536.tldr: Empirical results show that Omni-R1 achieves unified generative reasoning across a wide range of multimodal tasks, and Omni-R1-Zero can match or even surpass Omni-R1 on average, suggesting a promising direction for generative multimodal reasoning.

2601.09555.tldr: This work conducts a systematic investigation of PTQ under MXFP formats, encompassing over 7 PTQ algorithms, 15 evaluation benchmarks, and 3 LLM families, and provides practical guidance on adapting existing PTQ methods to MXFP quantization.

2601.09600.tldr: This work operationalizes Paulo Freire's theories of emancipatory pedagogy to develop a problem-posing framework for envisioning emancipatory IA platforms of the future.

2601.09603.tldr: This research combines the Branchformer architecture with SummaryMixing, which were first applied in speech recognition, along with a random quantization process, to achieve competitive performance when compared with other state-of-the-art models that use multi-head self-attention.

2601.09609.tldr: A Diverse Planning Branching method is introduced that strategically introduces divergence at the planning phase based on diversity variation, alongside a group-aware diversity reward to encourage distinct trajectories in large language models.

2601.09613.tldr: A novel benchmark, CogRail, is introduced, which integrates curated open-source datasets with cognitively driven question-answer annotations to support spatio-temporal reasoning and prediction, and a joint fine-tuning framework is proposed that significantly enhances model performance by enabling targeted adaptation to domain-specific reasoning demands.

2601.09620.tldr: The findings show that not all AI disclosures lead to a transparency dilemma, but instead reflect a trade-off between readers'desire for more transparency and their trust in AI-assisted news content.

2601.09624.tldr: Circuit-guided Unlearning Difficulty (CUD), a metric that assigns each sample a continuous difficulty score using circuit-level signals, is proposed, which takes a first step toward a principled, fine-grained, and interpretable analysis of unlearning difficulty; and motivates the development of unlearning methods grounded in model mechanisms.

2601.09626.tldr: Two gradient-free, LLM-driven closed-loop methods are introduced: Prompt-to-Optimizer (P2O), which uses an LLM to propose the code for small neural-network-based protocols, which are then trained by an inner loop, and Prompt-to-Protocol (P2P), which simply writes an explicit function for the current and its scalar parameters.

2601.09636.tldr: H Hierarchical Implicit Intent Alignment for Personalized GUI Agent (PersonalAlign) is highlighted, a new agent task that requires agents to leverage long-term user records as persistent context to resolve omitted preferences in vague instructions and anticipate latent routines by user state for proactive assistance.

2601.09680.tldr: This work introduces a minimally supervised agentic AI framework that autonomously monitors, analyses, and responds to disruptions across extended supply networks, establishing a foundational step toward building resilient, proactive, and autonomous supply chains capable of managing disruptions across deep-tier networks.

2601.09684.tldr: Ortho-LoRA dynamically projects conflicting task gradients onto the orthogonal complement of each other within the intrinsic LoRA subspace, effectively mitigates task interference and recovering 95\% of the performance gap between multi-task and single-task baselines with negligible computational overhead.

2601.09692.tldr: This work introduces Routing with Generated Data (RGD), a challenging setting in which routers are trained exclusively on generated queries and answers produced from high-level task descriptions by generator LLMs, and proposes CASCAL, a novel query-only router that estimates model correctness through consensus voting and identifies model-specific skill niches via hierarchical clustering.

2601.09694.tldr: This work introduces agent-guided pruning, where a foundation model acts as an adaptive pruning agent to intelligently select which layers to prune at each iteration while preserving critical knowledge pathways, and demonstrates that foundation models can effectively guide the compression of other foundation models.

2601.09703.tldr: A knowledge-infused framework named ShortCoder is proposed, which optimizes code generation efficiency while preserving semantic equivalence and readability, and introduces a fine-tuning strategy that injects conciseness awareness into the base LLMs.

2601.09706.tldr: Evaluation on arithmetic tasks shows that the proposed approach outperforms baselines across numerical formats, tasks, and operand lengths, indicating that explicitly encoding numerical value is an effective and efficient way to improve fundamental numerical robustness in language models.

2405.19631.tldr: An intelligent routing system for SDOH coding that uses a language model router to direct medical record data to open-source LLMs that demonstrate optimal performance on specific SDOH codes is introduced.

2407.18454.tldr: A systematic survey that clarifies the definitions of fairness as they apply to LMs and introduces a novel taxonomy that categorizes these concepts based on their transformer architecture: encoder‐only, decoder‐only, and encoder‐decoder LMs.

2410.03055.tldr: This paper proposes a novel, more permissive approach to propagate information flow labels through LLM queries to propagate only the labels of the samples that were influential in generating the model output and to eliminate the labels of unnecessary inputs.

2412.17228.tldr: MatchMiner-AI demonstrates an openly accessible, privacy-preserving approach to distilling a clinical trial matching AI pipeline from LLM-generated synthetic EHR data.

2502.01930.tldr: This work develops two novel distributionally robust direct preference optimization (DPO) algorithms, namely, Wasserstein DPO (WDPO) and Kullback-Leibler DPO (KLDPO), and characterize the sample complexity of learning the optimal policy parameters for WDPO and KLDPO.

2502.04675.tldr: This work conducts Human-Human, Human-AI, and AI-AI experiments to investigate the potential of recursive self-critiquing for AI supervision, and highlights recursive critique as a promising approach for scalable AI oversight.

2502.07115.tldr: This work model LLM inference with KV cache constraints theoretically and proposes a novel batching and scheduling algorithm that minimizes inference latency while effectively managing the KV cache's memory, and demonstrates the algorithm's strong empirical performance by comparing it to the hindsight optimal in a synthetic dataset.

2502.14131.tldr: The novelty of the approach lies in introducing the Empirical Risk Minimization (ERM) based IRL/DDC framework, which circumvents the need for explicit state transition probability estimation in the Bellman equation and has the potential to be scaled to high-dimensional, infinite state spaces.

2503.03283.tldr: A framework for investigating the internal inference impacted by input data augmentations is proposed and a way of single-class sensitivity analysis where the candidates are filtered according to their matching to prediction bias generated by targeted damaging of the activations is introduced.

2504.03716.tldr: The results indicate that current LLMs can introduce inequalities in real-world allocation scenarios, underscoring the urgent need for rigorous fairness evaluation and human oversight before their use in high-stakes decision-making.

2504.11788.tldr: This work enhances web agents with an explicit rollback mechanism, enabling the agent to revert back to a previous state in its navigation trajectory, giving models the flexibility to directly control the search process, leading to an effective and efficient web navigation method.

2505.11594.tldr: This work designs an accurate and efficient 8-bit attention for both forward and backward propagation, and pioneer low-bit attention to training tasks, to explore whether low-bit attention can be effectively applied to training tasks.

2505.21441.tldr: The strategy builds on foundational results from nonparametric statistics and spectral graph theory to learn a low-dimensional embedding of the model that optimally represents relationships in the data to provide exact and approximate solutions to the decoding problem via constrained optimization, split relabeling, and nearest neighbors regression.

2505.22310.tldr: It is made the surprising discovery that forget-set accuracy can recover from around 50% post-unlearning to nearly 100% with fine-tuning on just the retain set -- i.e., zero examples of the forget set.

2505.23281.tldr: MathArena is a new benchmark based on the following key insight: recurring math competitions provide a stream of high-quality, challenging problems that can be used for real-time evaluation of LLMs, and evaluating models as soon as new problems are released effectively eliminates the risk of contamination.

2506.21621.tldr: This work presents the Open Proof Corpus (OPC), a dataset comprising over 5,000 human-evaluated proofs produced by state-of-the-art LLMs, and is the first to include a substantial number of correct, LLM-generated solutions to problems from prestigious mathematics competitions such as the USAMO and IMO.

2507.03870.tldr: This work introduces AIProbe, a novel black-box differential testing framework to validate autonomous agents under varied and challenging environment configurations and demonstrates its broad applicability to both model-free and model-based agents operating in discrete and continuous domains.

2507.15143.tldr: A hybrid simulation framework that integrates agent-based modeling, reinforcement learning, reinforcement learning, supervised learning, and graph neural networks is developed, suggesting that efficient and sustainable mobility in extreme urban forms is achievable, provided adaptive AI systems, intelligent infrastructure, and real-time feedback mechanisms are implemented.

2508.20282.tldr: A novel prompt and user trait leakage attack against WRAs that only leverages their network-level metadata (i.e., visited IP addresses and their timings) is demonstrated and recovers over 73\% of the functional and domain knowledge of user prompts.

2509.02097.tldr: JudgeAgent is a knowledge-driven and dynamic evaluation framework for large language models that leverages LLM agents equipped with context graphs to traverse knowledge structures systematically for question generation and adopts a difficulty-adaptive and multi-turn interview mechanism.

2509.23870.tldr: This work proposes a novel objective where the actor is trained to simultaneously function as a classifier that separates good and bad actions, which mitigates negative gradient interference and improve the generalization performance.

2510.02692.tldr: In inverse noise correction, a novel algorithm to improve the quality of pre-trained flow models without explicit rewards, is proposed and empirically evaluated on text-to-image(T2I) generation, layout generation, molecule generation and unconditional image generation.

2510.05465.tldr: The Value ALignment Benchmark (VAL-Bench) is introduced, which measures the consistency in language model belief expressions in response to real-life value-laden prompts, and stresses the importance of research towards training belief consistency in modern LLMs.

2510.12604.tldr: COINS is proposed, an item representation enhancement approach based on fused alignment of semantic IDs that uses RQ-OPQ encoding to quantize item content and collaborative information, followed by a two-step alignment: RQ encoding transfers shared collaborative signals across items, while OPQ encoding learns differentiated information of items.

2510.24039.tldr: An end-to-end differentiable framework is designed that enables us to solve discrete constrained optimization problems with neural networks and can consistently outperform neural baselines in cardinality-constrained optimization.

2511.07920.tldr: Results demonstrate that real-time-optimized diffusion-based architectures, combined with clinically grounded task design, can support feasible online imagined speech decoding for communication-oriented BCI applications in aphasia.

2511.20696.tldr: Experiments demonstrate that ProNECL effec-tively balances knowledge retention and adaptability, achieving superior performance in cross-subject continual EEG decoding tasks.

2512.23860.tldr: A novel task named lifelong domain adaptive 3D HPE is proposed, and an innovative Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) framework is presented, which incorporates 3D pose generators, a 2D pose discriminator, and a 3D pose estimator, which effectively mitigates domain shifts and aligns original and augmented poses.

2601.01014.tldr: It is argued that the collapse of deep Transformers is fundamentally a geometric problem, and an evaluation protocol for Transformers exceeding 100 layers is outlined to test the hypothesis that geometry, rather than depth itself, is the key limiting factor in deep representation learning.

2601.06336.tldr: This work trains language models to make probabilistic forecasts from causally masked information, using proper scoring rules as the reward function once events resolve, enabling scalable outcome-based supervision in open-world prediction.

2601.08499.tldr: EfficientFSL, a query-only fine-tuning framework tailored specifically for few-shot classification with ViT, achieves competitive performance while significantly reducing computational overhead, demonstrating its effectiveness in real-world applications.

2601.09100.tldr: DScheLLM is proposed, a dynamic scheduling approach that leverages fine-tuned large language models within a dual-system (fast-slow) reasoning architecture to address disturbances of different scales in dynamic environments.

2601.09236.tldr: R4 is introduced, a new rating-based RL method that employs a novel ranking mean squared error (rMSE) loss, which treats teacher-provided ratings as ordinal targets and offers formal guarantees: its solution set is provably minimal and complete under mild assumptions.

2601.09714.tldr: Results reveal varied performance across research domains, with high-performing workflows maintaining feasibility without sacrificing creativity, and support the view that carefully designed multi-stage agentic workflows can advance AI-assisted research ideation.

2601.09717.tldr: This study presents a large language model-based extraction pipeline, SALP-CG, for classifying and grading privacy risks in online conversational health data, and concluded health-data classification and grading rules in accordance with GB/T 39725-2020.

2601.09720.tldr: A demonstration of uncertainty-aware dynamic KGs, a framework that combines dynamic construction of evolving KGs, confidence scoring and uncertainty-aware retrieval, and an interactive interface for reliable and interpretable QA.

2601.09721.tldr: Evaluated LLM safety under parental anxiety-driven adversarial pressures in pediatric consultations across models and platforms shows safety depends on alignment and architecture over scale, with smaller models outperforming larger.

2601.09722.tldr: An annotation framework is presented that demonstrates how a multilingual LLM pretrained on a large corpus can be used as a teacher model to distill the expert knowledge needed for tagging medical texts in Polish.

2601.09723.tldr: SagaScale is introduced, a realistic, scalable, and high-quality long-context benchmark built from full-length novels that yields key insights, including direct supplying the full context to the LLM can outperform other methods by a large margin.

2601.09726.tldr: This work model LLM inference as a probabilistic memory process governed by exponential decay, and proposes probabilistic memory prompting, a lightweight strategy that shapes evidence integration to mimic human-like memory decay, leading to improved long-horizon reasoning performance.

2601.09727.tldr: This work frames mechanistic synthesis as a graph-constrained multi-hop reasoning problem over literature-derived concept graphs, and introduces a behavioral framework that measures symbolic reasoning depth, mechanistic diversity, and grounding stability.

2601.09728.tldr: The Stage Token for Introduction Generation (STIG) converts the multiple stages of the original workflow into explicit stage signals and outperforms traditional agentic workflows and other baselines on metrics of semantic similarity and sentence-level structural rationality.

2601.09729.tldr: This work presents a hybrid summarization framework that combines extractive and abstractive techniques to produce concise and factually reliable Reuters-style summaries from the ECTSum dataset, and highlights complementary trade offs between approaches.

2601.09730.tldr: It is anticipated that research on clinical document metadata extraction will continue to expand into richer document metadata representations and integrate further into clinical applications and workflows and highlight gaps.

2601.09733.tldr: Empirical results demonstrate that ODA-driven datasets significantly improve both domain-specific reasoning and general utility while achieving superior data efficiency, validating a transition toward data-centric AI where transparent evaluation serves as the primary engine for engineering high-quality training data.

2601.09734.tldr: This work develops the Hallucination Diagnosis Generator (HDG), an automated pipeline that systematically generates high-quality training samples with rich diagnostic metadata from raw corpora through multi-dimensional augmentation strategies including controlled fact fabrication and reasoning chain perturbation, and trains a 4-billion-parameter hallucination diagnosis model.

2601.09736.tldr: This thesis proposes a novel approach that uses Q-Learning on top of LGP, Reinforced Linear Genetic Programming (RLGP) to learn the optimal register-action assignments, and introduces a new framework "linear-gp" written in memory-safe Rust that allows for extensive experimentation for future works.

2601.09740.tldr: This work develops a formally verified safety framework for Connected and Autonomous Vehicles that integrates Barrier Certificates with interpretable traffic conflict metrics, specifically Time-to-Collision (TTC) as a spatio-temporal safety metric.

2601.09745.tldr: A case study showing that recent advances in artificial intelligence make it possible to retain many of the benefits of formal specification while substantially reducing these costs, and enables early validation, explicit invariants, and correctness by design, while significantly reducing development effort.

2601.09746.tldr: A novel Multi-Agent Cooperative Learning framework to address cross-modal alignment collapse in vision-language models when handling out-of-distribution (OOD) concepts, which enables multi-agent feature space name learning and incorporates a context exchange enhanced few-shot learning algorithm.

2601.09749.tldr: R-LAM is proposed, a reproducibility-constrained framework for applying Large Action Models to scientific workflow automation that improves reproducibility success rates and execution reliability compared to unconstrained LLM-based agents, while retaining adaptive control over workflow execution.

2601.09750.tldr: This paper presents SAGE, a specialized conversational AI interface based on the OPACA framework for tool discovery and execution, and implemented a number of task-solving strategies, making use of agentic concepts and prompting methods in various degrees of complexity.

2601.09753.tldr: It is argued for a social, pragmatist epistemology and a newly articulated norm of Critically Engaged Pragmatism to enjoin scientific communities to vigorously scrutinize the purposes and purpose-specific reliability of AI science evaluation tools.

2601.09755.tldr: This paper shows how to combine neuromorphic computing hardware, exemplified by the Loihi2 processor used in conjunction with event-based cameras, for sensing and real-time perception and interaction with a local AI compute cluster (GPUs) for high-level language processing, cognition, and task planning.

2601.09756.tldr: It is concluded that synthetic augmentation is effective for expanding exposure but is complementary, not substitutive, for safety-critical veterinary de-identification.

2601.09757.tldr: This essay draws on cases in which AI decision-making has been challenged in courts to show how concepts of due process and equal protection can be recuperated in a modern AI era, and even integrated into AI to provide for better oversight and accountability.

2601.09760.tldr: This paper proposes a new type of knowledge conflict -- Tool-Memory Conflict (TMC), where the internal parametric knowledge contradicts with the external tool knowledge for tool-augmented LLMs.

2601.09762.tldr: RAFT is proposed, a framework for requirements auto-formalization and compliance test generation via explicating tacit regulatory knowledge from multiple LLMs and integrating it into three artifacts: a domain meta-model, a formal requirements representation, and testability constraints.

2601.09765.tldr: A general framework for thinking about the existential risk of AI systems is developed, and a taxonomy of survival stories, in which humanity survives into the far future is constructed, arguing that different survival stories face different challenges.

2601.09770.tldr: GUI-Eyes, a reinforcement learning framework for active visual perception in GUI tasks, is presented, which introduces a progressive perception strategy that decomposes decision-making into coarse exploration and fine-grained grounding, coordinated by a two-level policy.

2601.09771.tldr: PCN-Rec is presented, a proof-carrying negotiation pipeline that separates natural-language reasoning from deterministic enforcement, and achieves a 98.55% pass rate on feasible users on MovieLens-100K with governance constraints.

2601.09772.tldr: An experiment where participants could spend part of their own endowment to reduce the earnings of peers who had previously completed a real-effort task with or without LLM support provides the first behavioral evidence that the efficiency gains of LLMs come at the cost of social sanctions.

2601.09773.tldr: This paper proposes an architectural enhancement that aggregates multiple PolyLUT sub-neurons via an adder, significantly reducing LUT consumption and lowering inference latency, and introduces a non-greedy training algorithm that optimizes neuron connectivity by selectively pruning less significant inputs and strategically regrowing more effective ones.

2601.09806.tldr: This work utilizes FGSM to generate adversarial noise targeting an identity classifier and employs a diffusion model with reverse diffusion to enhance imperceptibility through Gaussian smoothing and adaptive brightness correction, thereby facilitating synthetic adversarial patch evasion.

2601.09809.tldr: This study examines the potential of quantum-assisted federated learning, which could cut the number of parameters in classical models by polylogarithmic factors and thus lessen training overhead and point to the potential of leveraging quantum computing within a federated learning context to strengthen FL capabilities of edge devices.

2601.09814.tldr: EfficientNet-B0 provided a more balanced and computationally efficient performance compared to DenseNet121, making it a strong candidate for clinical deployment and the integration of explainability techniques enhances transparency and trustworthiness in AI-assisted pediatric pneumonia diagnosis.

2601.09853.tldr: A semi-automated pipeline is developed to curate MedRedFlag, a dataset of 1100+ questions sourced from Reddit that require redirection, and analysis reveals that LLMs often fail to redirect problematic questions, even when the problematic premise is detected, and provide answers that could lead to suboptimal medical decision making.

2601.09855.tldr: This work presents a novel sequential test-time scaling method, Min-Seek, which improves model accuracy significantly over a wide range of induced thoughts, stabilizing the accuracy of sequential scaling, and removing the need for reasoning length fine-tuning.

2601.09858.tldr: This work presents a reinforcement learning framework that casts scientific outline construction as a long-horizon planning problem over hierarchical document structures, and introduces a benchmark for scientific paper generation that evaluates document planning, input utilization, reference faithfulness, outline organization, and content-level factual accuracy.

2601.09865.tldr: This work proposes an integrated framework combining GPTQ-based quantization, low-rank adaptation (LoRA), and a specialized data distillation process to significantly reduce model size and complexity while preserving or enhancing task-specific performance.

2601.09869.tldr: This scoping review maps ethically oriented work on anthropomorphising LLM-based CAs across five databases and three preprint repositories and finds convergence on attribution-based definitions but substantial divergence in operationalization, a predominantly risk-forward normative framing, and limited empirical work that links observed interaction effects to actionable governance guidance.

2601.09871.tldr: The approach suggests that the role and value of complementarity lie not in providing a stand-alone measure of relative predictive accuracy, but in helping calibrate decision-making to the reliability of AI-supported processes.

2601.09879.tldr: MedVL-SAM2 is proposed, a unified 3D medical multimodal model that concurrently supports report generation, VQA, and multi-paradigm segmentation, including semantic, referring, and interactive segmentation, and demonstrates that high-level semantic reasoning and precise 3D localization can be jointly achieved within a unified 3D medical VLM.

2601.09881.tldr: Transition Matching Distillation (TMD), a novel framework for distilling video diffusion models into efficient few-step generators, outperforms existing distilled models under comparable inference costs in terms of visual fidelity and prompt adherence.

2601.09883.tldr: An Information-Flow-Orchestrated Multi-Agent Paradigm via Agent-to-Agent (A2A) Communication from CORAL is proposed, in which a dedicated information flow orchestrator continuously monitors task progress and dynamically coordinates other agents through the A2A toolkit using natural language, without relying on predefined workflows.

2601.09902.tldr: This work proposes a novel contrastive loss function which is able to maintain the advantages of other contrastive learning-based approaches (robustness to imbalanced data) but can also generalise to zero-day attacks.

2601.09913.tldr: The empirical probes demonstrate that CMA is a necessary architectural primitive for long-horizon agents while highlighting open challenges around latency, drift, and interpretability.

2601.09921.tldr: This work presents the first scalable, neural-network-based parallel decoding framework that simultaneously achieves SOTA accuracy and the stringent throughput required for real-time quantum error correction.

2601.09923.tldr: This work introduces Single-Shot Planning for CUAs, where a trusted planner generates a complete execution graph with conditional branches before any observation of potentially malicious content, providing provable control flow integrity guarantees against arbitrary instruction injections.

2601.09929.tldr: This paper introduces a comprehensive operational framework for hallucination management, built on a continuous improvement cycle driven by root cause awareness, and provides a systematic, scalable methodology for building trustworthy generative AI systems in regulated environments.

2601.09933.tldr: The proposed FGSMDICNN model attains 99.44% accuracy while outperforming other existing approaches such as Custom Deep Neural Network (DCNN) while outperforming other existing approaches such as Custom Deep Neural Network (DCNN).

2601.09972.tldr: LabourLawLLM is presented, a legal large language model tailored to Chinese labor law that consistently outperforms general-purpose and existing legal-specific LLMs across task categories and provides a scalable approach for building specialized LLMs in other legal subfields.

2601.09974.tldr: SPRInG, a novel semi-parametric framework designed for effective continual personalization, is introduced, which employs drift-driven selective adaptation, which utilizes a likelihood-based scoring function to identify high-novelty interactions.

2601.09980.tldr: The results show that agents based on reasoning models like OpenAI's o3 and GPT5 consistently succeeded at completing this ALD process optimization task, however, significant run-to-run variability is observed due to the non deterministic nature of the model's response.

2601.10010.tldr: A novel benchmark for evaluating the Video Event Relation Hallucination is introduced, named VERHallu, which focuses on causal, temporal, and subevent relations between events, encompassing three types of tasks: relation classification, question answering, and counterfactual question answering.

2601.10011.tldr: Mozo-SQL is presented, a training-free framework that addresses issues through two simple ideas: structured decomposition and experience-aware self-correction, and sets a new state of the art among open, zero-fine-tuning methods, while using over 10 times fewer resources than prior TTS approaches.

2601.10018.tldr: This work shows how foundation models can enhance technology support for older adults by addressing age-related communication barriers and develops a pipeline using large language models to generate the first synthetic dataset of how older adults request tech support (OATS).

2601.10025.tldr: A framework that models LLM personality via Jungian psychological types, integrating three mechanisms: a dominant-auxiliary coordination mechanism for coherent core expression, a reinforcement-compensation mechanism for temporary adaptation to context, and a reflection mechanism that drives long-term personality evolution is presented.

2601.10029.tldr: Proximal Sequence Policy Optimization (PSPO), a process-aware, sequence-level policy optimization method that aligns optimization with agent--environment interaction, is introduced, validating the effectiveness of the adaptive agentic framework and optimization strategy.

2601.10031.tldr: This work focuses on a representative application of large deformations, the stretch bending problem, and proposes FilDeep, a Fidelity-based Deep Learning framework for large Deformation of elastic-plastic solids, which is likely the first DL framework for large deformation problems using MF data.

2601.10038.tldr: It is argued that philosophy of science offers essential tools for navigating AI's integration into astronomy--conceptual clarity about what "understanding" means, critical examination of assumptions about data and discovery, and frameworks for evaluating AI's roles across different research contexts.

2601.10061.tldr: This work proposes CoF-T2I, a model that integrates CoF reasoning into T2I generation via progressive visual refinement, where intermediate frames act as explicit reasoning steps and the final frame is taken as output.

2601.10073.tldr: ReaMIL (Reasoning- and Evidence-Aware MIL), a multiple instance learning approach for whole-slide histopathology that adds a light selection head to a strong MIL backbone, is introduced and accuracy alongside MSK, AUKC, and contiguity is reported for rigorous evaluation of model behavior on WSIs.

2601.10079.tldr: Sparse-RL incorporates Sparsity-Aware Rejection Sampling and Importance-based Reweighting to correct the off-policy bias introduced by compression-induced information loss, and inherently implements sparsity-aware training, significantly enhancing model robustness during sparse inference deployment.

2601.10088.tldr: This work uses the OpenRouter platform, which is an AI inference provider across a wide variety of LLMs, to analyze over 100 trillion tokens of real-world LLM interactions across tasks, geographies, and time, and identifies foundational cohorts: early users whose engagement persists far longer than later cohorts.

2601.10090.tldr: This paper proposes difficulty-guided sampling (DGS) to bridge the target gap between the distillation objective and the downstream task, therefore improving the performance of dataset distillation and highlights the broader potential of difficulty for diverse downstream tasks.

2601.10092.tldr: Experiments on length of stay prediction using Intensive Care Unit (ICU) data demonstrate that LeMoF consistently outperforms existing state-of-the-art multimodal fusion techniques across various encoder configurations, and confirmed that level-wise integration is a key factor in achieving robust predictive performance across various clinical conditions.

2601.10094.tldr: V-Zero, a general post-training framework that facilitates self-improvement using exclusively unlabeled images and establishes a co-evolutionary loop by instantiating two distinct roles: a Questioner and a Solver, demonstrates the potential of self-improvement in multimodal systems.

2601.10103.tldr: This paper proposes FlowAct-R1, a framework specifically designed for real-time interactive humanoid video generation, built upon a MMDiT architecture that achieves exceptional behavioral vividness and perceptual realism, while maintaining robust generalization across diverse character styles.

2601.10104.tldr: Experiments on SOTA MLLMs show that although end-to-end models achieve strong extraction performance, they consistently fail to refuse illegible inputs, instead producing confident but invalid outputs, highlighting a critical gap in current MLLMs.

2601.10108.tldr: This work proposes the "Fish-in-the-Ocean"(FITO) paradigm, which requires models to construct explicit cross-modal evidence chains within native scientific documents, and introduces "No Evidence, No Score", scoring predictions when grounded to verifiable anchors and diagnosing evidence quality via matching, relevance, and logic.

2601.10112.tldr: The Repository Intelligence Graph is introduced, a deterministic, evidence backed architectural map that represents buildable components, aggregators, runners, tests, external packages, and package managers, connected by explicit dependency and coverage edges that trace back to concrete build and test definitions.

2601.10114.tldr: Experiments show that the proposed Scheduled Checkpoint Distillation (SCD) method consistently outperforms existing distillation approaches, allowing the student model to match or even exceed the performance of its fine-tuned teacher on domain-specific tasks.

2601.10120.tldr: TopoDIM, a framework for one-shot Topology generation with Diverse Interaction Modes, designed for decentralized execution to enhance adaptability and privacy, enables agents to autonomously construct heterogeneous communication without iterative coordination, achieving token efficiency and improved task performance.

2601.10122.tldr: The paper summarizes the critical technical pathways supporting high-quality role-playing, including psychological scale-driven character modeling, memory-augmented prompting mechanisms, and motivation-situation-based behavioral decision control, and outlines future development directions of role-playing agents, including personality evolution modeling, multi-agent collaborative narrative, multimodal immersive interaction, and integration with cognitive neuroscience.

2601.10129.tldr: LaViT compels the student to autoregressively reconstruct the teacher's visual semantics and attention trajectories prior to text generation, employing a curriculum sensory gating mechanism to prevent shortcut learning and significantly enhances visual grounding.

2601.10130.tldr: SDP (Selective-Discovery-and-Prune), which discovers the top-$k$ FDs ranked by redundancy count and improves SDP with three optimizations: ordering attributes by partition cardinality, using pairwise statistics in a Partition Cardinality Matrix to tighten bounds, and a global scheduler to explore promising branches first.

2405.09037.tldr: Salient Sparse Federated Learning (SSFL), a streamlined approach for sparse federated learning with efficient communication that consistently improves the accuracy sparsity trade off, achieving more than 20\% relative error reduction on CIFAR-10 compared to the strongest sparse baseline.

2406.17216.tldr: While unlearning methods show some signs of being useful to efficiently remove poisoned data without having to retrain, this work suggests that these methods are not yet ``ready for prime time,''and currently provide limited benefit over retraining.

2409.11277.tldr: It is shown (against recent trends in philosophy of science) that ML model-building is mostly indifferent to domain-theory, even if the model remains theory-laden in a weak sense, which is called theory-infection.

2410.01944.tldr: This work exploits the properties of high-dimensional orthogonality to identify a robust and effective boundary in cone space for separating clean and noisy samples and proposes One-Step Anti-noise (OSA), a model-agnostic noisy label mitigation paradigm that employs an estimator model and a scoring function to assess the noise level of input pairs through just one-step inference.

2410.10336.tldr: Chain of Mathematically Annotated Thought (CoMAT) is presented, which enhances reasoning through two stages: Symbolic Conversion and Reasoning Execution, offering a transparent reasoning process for complex mathematical tasks.

2412.07990.tldr: This work examines how to learn a penalty function associated with unsafe behaviors using multiple forms of human feedback, by optimizing both the query state and feedback format, in an iterative, two-phase approach.

2502.12128.tldr: The core idea of LaM-SLidE is the introduction of identifier representations (IDs) that enable the retrieval of entity properties and entity composition from latent system representations, thus fostering traceability.

2502.12965.tldr: This work divides the methods in this area based on the constraints that define the kind of distribution shift and the corresponding problem formulation, i.e. learning with the Universum, zero-shot learning, and open-set learning.

2503.06195.tldr: A systematic literature review of 90 studies is conducted, summarizing current findings and outlining areas for further investigation, which calls for larger and longer evaluations, stronger audit and verification assets, broader coverage across the software life cycle, and adaptive assistance under user control.

2503.17523.tldr: It is shown that large language models fail to update beliefs in a Bayesian way but can be taught to do so by mimicking a normative Bayesian model, which yields better predictions and transferable reasoning skills across tasks.

2505.08814.tldr: An investigation was carried out on the relationships between modified decision/condition coverage and dataset size, and three potential future directions are proposed to further contribute to the security testing of DNN Models.

2505.20323.tldr: PMA-TTS enables research on timeline extraction, temporal reasoning, survival modeling and event forecasting from narrative text, and offers broad diagnostic and demographic coverage, and offers broad diagnostic and demographic coverage.

2505.20355.tldr: Granular Low-Rank Adaptation (GraLoRA) is introduced, a novel structure that partitions weight matrices into sub-blocks, each with its own low-rank adapter that overcomes LoRA's limitations, effectively increases the representational capacity, and more closely approximates FFT behavior.

2506.10407.tldr: An STP-based CNN framework is developed that extends convolutional computation to irregular and cross-dimensional data domains and inherently avoids zero or other artificial padding, thereby eliminating redundant information and boundary artifacts commonly present in conventional convolutional neural networks.

2506.14375.tldr: The IntelliLung project develops a system in close collaboration with healthcare professionals that is aligned with real-world clinical objectives and designed with future deployment in mind, and introduces a clinically grounded reward function based on ventilator-free days and physiological targets.

2506.18434.tldr: This study introduces the first structured benchmark to assess the robustness and efficiency of transfer learning strategies for FMs compared with convolutional neural networks in predicting COVID-19 patient outcomes from chest X-rays, offering empirical guidance for AI deployment in clinical workflows.

2507.10646.tldr: This work introduces CodeAssistBench (CAB), the first benchmark for evaluating multi-turn, project-grounded programming assistance at scale, and provides a scalable, reproducible framework for advancing research in multi-turn, codebase-grounded programming agents.

2507.20923.tldr: Multi-heuristics for MOCOP via Pareto-Grid-guided Evolution of LLMs (MPaGE), a novel enhancement of the Simple Evolutionary Multiobjective Optimization (SEMO) framework that leverages LLMs and Pareto Front Grid (PFG) technique that achieves competitive results to traditional Multi-objective evolutionary algorithms (MOEAs), with significantly faster runtime.

2508.01343.tldr: This paper proposes UEChecker, a deep learning-based tool that utilizes a call graph and a Graph Convolutional Network to detect unchecked external call vulnerabilities and shows that the tool consistently outperforms these models in terms of accuracy.

2508.10956.tldr: This work introduces a systematic evaluation framework comprising images of three representative types, three reasoning levels of increasing complexity, and four object property dimensions, informed by prior work on common sense, and develops a procedure to instantiate this framework in two VQA object reasoning benchmarks.

2509.10222.tldr: CARENLI, a compartmentalised agentic framework that routes each premise-statement pair to a reasoning family and then applies a specialised solver with explicit verification and targeted refinement, supports compartmentalisation plus verification as a practical route to more reliable and auditable clinical inference.

2509.10798.tldr: Judge Q is proposed, a novel training method which incorporates a soft token list which can be seamlessly integrated into existing open-source models with minimal training overhead, thereby enhancing performance in KV cache eviction scenarios.

2509.13620.tldr: DeFINO (Derivative-based Fisher-score Informed Neural Operator) is proposed, a reduced-order, derivative-informed training framework that captures critical sensitivity information directly informed by observational data, significantly reducing computational expense.

2509.23773.tldr: A Graph Neural Network regression model is proposed to estimate entity-level knowledgeability scores for triplets by leveraging their neighborhood scores, and the predicted knowledgeability enables us to prioritize checking less well-known triplets, thereby maximizing knowledge coverage under the same labeling budget.

2510.01444.tldr: DUPL is introduced, a dual-uncertainty guided policy learning approach for multimodal RLVR that quantifies and leverages both perceptual uncertainty and output uncertainty to guide policy updates, demonstrating that dual-uncertainty guided policy learning is an effective and generalizable approach for multimodal RLVR.

2510.07745.tldr: This work enables parallel TTS for latent reasoning models by addressing the lack of probabilistic signals for advanced trajectory aggregation and introducing two uncertainty-inspired stochastic strategies: Monte Carlo Dropout and Additive Gaussian Noise.

2510.20721.tldr: The need for more user-centered studies to measure LLMs'ability to help users while preserving privacy, and for improving alignment between LLMs and users in estimating perceived privacy and utility, is discussed.

2510.22655.tldr: This work proposes an unsupervised representation learning method that replaces augmentations by generating views by generating views using orthonormal bases and overcomplete frames, and shows that embeddings learned from orthonormal and overcomplete spaces reside on distinct manifolds.

2510.25626.tldr: A framework for assessing LM reasoning efficiency through the lens of logic programming is proposed, introducing a simple method to align proofs written in natural language -- as generated by an LM -- with shortest proofs found by executing the logic program.

2511.00423.tldr: BOOM (Bootstrap Off-policy with WOrld Model), a framework that tightly integrates planning and off-policy learning through a bootstrap loop: the policy initializes the planner, and the planner refines actions to bootstrap the policy through behavior alignment.

2511.01891.tldr: Speculative Chunk-level based Rejection sampling (SCR) is designed, which generates responses in chunks and parallelly validates them via estimated thresholds within a sliding window, which significantly reduces computational overhead while maintaining high-quality generation.

2512.01242.tldr: This work studies abstract visual composition, in which identity is primarily determined by the spatial configuration and relations among a small set of geometric primitives, and proposes a constraint-guided framework that combines explicit geometric reasoning with neural semantics.

2512.13142.tldr: Empirical evidence is provided that LLMs lack coherent understanding of psychological constructs operating across multiple dimensions, particularly in domains where understanding what people cannot say determines whether support helps or harms.

2512.15372.tldr: This work proposes ICAR (Image Complexity-Aware Retrieval), an adaptive computation approach that enables vision transformers to use less compute for simple images whilst processing complex images through their full network depth, enabling sustainable scaling of vision-language systems.

2512.15729.tldr: TinyMyo is the first EMG FM for ultra-low power edge devices, enabling scalable and energy-efficient sensing for motor intent decoding, neuromuscular assessment, and biosignal driven human-machine interaction.

2512.21789.tldr: A look back at the first five years of SciCap and summarize the key technical and methodological lessons learned, which outline five major unsolved challenges and propose directions for the next phase of research in scientific figure captioning.

2601.00138.tldr: This work investigates whether confidence-based abstention provides reliable control over error rates in video question answering, and whether that control remains robust under distribution shift, and establishes two findings.

2601.03043.tldr: It is shown, both empirically and theoretically, that sparse attention can paradoxically increase end-to-end complexity: information loss often induces significantly longer sequences, a phenomenon the authors term ``Less is Less''(Lil).

2601.04377.tldr: Disco-RAG is proposed, a discourse-aware framework that explicitly injects discourse signals into the generation process and achieves state-of-the-art results on the benchmarks without fine-tuning, underscore the important role of discourse structure in advancing RAG systems.

2601.04741.tldr: TimeCast is presented, a dynamic prediction framework designed to adapt to these changes and provide accurate, real-time predictions of future event time while finding dynamic changes in data streams with a great reduction in computational time.

2601.05467.tldr: A Secure Transpiler and Executor of LLM-Generated Program (STELP), capable of executing LLM-generated code in a controlled and safe manner, and results demonstrate that the approach outperforms an existing method by a significant margin, particularly in its ability to safely execute risky code snippets.

2601.05656.tldr: HAG is proposed, a Hierarchical Agent Generation framework that formalizes population generation as a two-stage decision process, utilizing a World Knowledge Model to infer hierarchical conditional probabilities to construct the Topic-Adaptive Tree, achieving macro-level distribution alignment.

2601.06540.tldr: Comparative evaluations against random and clustering-based experience replay methods demonstrate that SODACER achieves faster convergence, improved sample efficiency, and a superior bias-variance trade-off, while maintaining safe system trajectories, validated via the Friedman test.

2601.08847.tldr: RIKER (Retrieval Intelligence and Knowledge Extraction Rating) is presented, both a benchmark and a replicable methodology based on paradigm inversion - generating documents from known ground truth rather than extracting ground truth from documents.

2601.09421.tldr: This work investigates BabyLMs, compact BERT-like models trained on small and mutable corpora that can approximate bias acquisition and learning dynamics of larger models, and demonstrates that BabyLMs can serve as an effective sandbox for large-scale LMs, reducing pre-training costs from over 500 GPU-hours to under 30 GPU-hours.

2601.09667.tldr: This work introduces MATTRL, a framework that injects structured textual experience into multi-agent deliberation at inference time and offers a stable, effective and efficient path to distribution-shift-robust multi-agent reasoning without tuning.

2601.10137.tldr: Tree-Query is introduced, a tree-structured, multi-expert LLM framework that reduces pairwise causal discovery to a short sequence of queries about backdoor paths, (in)dependence, latent confounding, and causal direction, yielding interpretable judgments with robustness-aware confidence scores.

2601.10141.tldr: This work proposes safety-preserving fine-tuning (SPF), a lightweight approach that explicitly removes gradient components conflicting with the low-rank safety subspace, and shows that SPF guarantees utility convergence while bounding safety drift.

2601.10143.tldr: A drift-aware dataflow system that integrates machine learning-based adaptive control into the data curation process and provides a generalizable approach to adaptive data management and learning-guided workflow automation for financial data is presented.

2601.10148.tldr: This work investigates the application of Large Language Models to offline decision making tasks and proposes treating trajectories as a distinct modality, which can autoregressively predict future decisions within a cohesive framework the authors term DecisionLLM.

2601.10150.tldr: This study proposes a novel node classification contrast learning method called Simple Network Graph Comparative Learning (SNGCL), which employs a superimposed multilayer Laplace smoothing filter as a step in processing the data to obtain global and local feature smoothing matrices.

2601.10155.tldr: This work proposes LOOKAT, which applies product quantization and asymmetric distance computation, to transformer architecture by decomposing key vectors into subspaces, learning codebooks and computing attention tables via lookup tables, which transforms attention from memory-bound to compute-bound.

2601.10157.tldr: MMPG is proposed, a framework that constructs protein graphs from multiple perspectives and adaptively fuses them via Mixture of Experts (MoE) for PRL, and quantitatively verify that MoE automatically specializes experts in modeling distinct levels of interaction from individual representations, to pairwise inter-perspective synergies, and ultimately to a global consensus across all perspectives.

2601.10168.tldr: The proposed RAG-3DSG introduces re-shot guided uncertainty estimation, and devise an Object-level Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) that leverages low-uncertainty objects as semantic anchors to retrieve more reliable contextual knowledge, enabling a Vision-Language Model to rectify the predictions of uncertain objects and optimize the final 3DSG.

2601.10169.tldr: This study demonstrates how artificial neural agents acquire and utilize compositional generalization to describe previously unseen images by composing basic concepts into complex phrases using a codebook acquired during interaction in a multi-target coordination game.

2601.10173.tldr: Comprehensive evaluations show that ReasAlign achieves the best trade-off between security and utility, establishing a robust and practical defense against prompt injection attacks in real-world agentic systems.

2601.10191.tldr: This study presents a workflow for systematically evaluating information loss caused by downsampling in high-frequency time series and shows that shape-aware downsampling algorithms outperform standard decimation, as they better preserve peak structure and overall signal morphology.

2601.10193.tldr: GFM4GA, a novel graph foundation model for group anomaly detection that surpasses group anomaly detectors and GFMs for individual anomalies, achieving average improvements of 2.85% in AUROC and 2.55% in AUPRC.

2601.10201.tldr: Process Reward Learning (PRL) is proposed, which decomposes the entropy regularized reinforcement learning objective into intermediate steps, with rigorous process rewards that could be assigned to models accordingly, and could turn the outcome reward into process supervision signals, which helps better guide the exploration during RL optimization.

2601.10205.tldr: A unified benchmark spanning 12 Indian languages and four evaluation tasks: monolingual and cross-lingual persona-to-instruction retrieval, reverse retrieval from instruction to persona, and binary compatibility classification is presented.

2601.10212.tldr: The Paillier cryptosystem is applied to the SoReg (Social Regularization) model, which exploits both user's ratings and social relations, and secure addition and multiplication protocols to support secure computation on any arithmetic circuit, along with an optimal data packing scheme that is suitable for the polynomial computations of real values.

2601.10215.tldr: Topo-RAG is presented, a framework that challenges the assumption that"everything is text" and proposes a dual architecture that respects the topology of the data: the authors route fluid narrative through traditional dense retrievers, while tabular structures are processed by a Cell-Aware Late Interaction mechanism, preserving their spatial relationships.

2601.10222.tldr: First- and second-order optimization techniques in both deterministic and stochastic settings are reviewed, their adaptation to physics-constrained and data-driven SciML models are discussed, and practical strategies are illustrated through tutorial examples.

2601.10236.tldr: Five design patterns are distill: on-demand initiation, micro-suggestions, voice anchoring, audience scaffolds, and point-of-decision provenance, to guide authorship-preserving writing tools and tests two common design choices: persona-based coaching and style personalization.

2601.10242.tldr: It is suggested that while LTs offer a promising direction for scaling computational depth, they have yet to achieve the introspection required to truly link representation space and natural language.

2601.10245.tldr: TRIM (Targeted routing in multi-step reasoning tasks), which routes only critical steps, those likely to derail the solution, to larger models while letting smaller models handle routine continuations, demonstrating that step-level difficulty represents fundamental characteristics of reasoning.

2601.10251.tldr: This work investigates Sharpness-Aware Minimization from a spectral and geometric perspective and proposes an explicit eigenvector-aligned SAM (X-SAM), which corrects the gradient via orthogonal decomposition along the top eigenvector, enabling more direct and efficient regularization of the Hessian's maximum eigenvalue.

2601.10254.tldr: NoReGeo is presented, a novel benchmark designed to evaluate the intrinsic geometric understanding of large language models (LLMs) without relying on reasoning or algebraic computation, highlighting a significant gap in current LLMs'ability to natively grasp geometric concepts.

2601.10272.tldr: MoST is presented, a novel multimodal large language model that seamlessly integrates speech and text processing through the proposed Modality-Aware Mixture of Experts (MAMoE) architecture and represents the first fully open-source speech-text LLM built on a Mixture of Experts architecture.

2601.10274.tldr: A constrained optimization problem is formulated that maximizes a weighted average accuracy objective penalized by the mean system time, subject to architectural token-budget constraints and queue-stability conditions, and a projected gradient method with a computable global step-size bound is developed to guarantee convergence beyond the contractive regime.

2601.10306.tldr: This work establishes the Evidence-Augmented Reasoning paradigm, validating via Tree-Structured Evidence Sampling that precise evidence extraction is the decisive bottleneck for long-context reasoning, and introduces a specialized RL algorithm where a reward model computes a Group-Relative Evidence Reward.

2601.10338.tldr: The first large-scale empirical security analysis of this emerging ecosystem, collecting 42,447 skills from two major marketplaces and systematically analyzing 31,132 using SkillScan, a multi-stage detection framework integrating static analysis with LLM-based semantic classification reveals pervasive security risks.

2601.10342.tldr: This work proposes C-GRASP (Clinically-Grounded Reasoning for Affective Signal Processing), a guardrailed RAG-enhanced pipeline that decomposes HRV interpretation into eight traceable reasoning steps and transitions affective computing from black-box classification to transparent, evidence-based clinical decision support, paving the way for safer AI integration in biomedical engineering.

2601.10348.tldr: This work proposes Training-Trajectory-Aware Token Selection (T3S) to reconstruct the training objective at the token level, clearing the optimization path for yet-to-learn tokens.

2601.10349.tldr: The proposed Strategy-aware Surprise (SuS), a novel intrinsic motivation framework that uses pre-post prediction mismatch as a novelty signal for exploration in reinforcement learning, introduces two complementary components: Strategy Stability (SS) and Strategy Surprise (SuS).

2601.10373.tldr: A Frequency-aware Skip Estimation module that refines the $\epsilon$-prediction prior from a pre-trained latent diffusion model and aligns it with compressed latents at different timesteps via Frequency Decoupling Attention (FDA), and a lightweight consistency estimator enables fast two-step decoding by preserving the semantic trajectory of diffusion sampling.

2601.10386.tldr: A missing-aware multimodal survival framework that combines Computed Tomography, Whole-Slide Histopathology Images, and structured clinical variables for overall survival modeling in unresectable stage II-III NSCLC is presented.

2601.10406.tldr: ErrEval is proposed, a flexible and Error-aware Evaluation framework that enhances QG evaluation through explicit error diagnostics and effectively mitigates the overestimation of low-quality questions.

2601.10413.tldr: The development of LADFA, an end-to-end computational framework, which can process unstructured text in a given privacy policy, extract personal data flows and construct a personal data flow graph, and conduct analysis of the data flow graph to facilitate insight discovery is presented.

2601.10416.tldr: LLMdoctor is introduced, a novel framework for efficient test-time alignment that operates via a patient-doctor paradigm that integrates token-level reward acquisition with token-level flow-guided preference optimization (TFPO) to steer a large, frozen patient LLM with a smaller, specialized doctor model.

2601.10421.tldr: An assessment at each of Marr's three levels suggests the claim LMs serve as model systems is clearly not true at the implementation level, poorly motivated at the algorithmic-representational level, and problematic at the computational theory level.

2601.10436.tldr: This paper introduces a structured, iterative methodology leveraging LLMs to optimize knowledge acquisition, automate ontology artifact generation, and enable continuous refinement cycles that highlights the transformative potential of integrating LLMs into ontology development.

2601.10440.tldr: The AgentGuardian is introduced, a novel security framework that governs and protects AI agent operations by enforcing context-aware access-control policies and mitigates hallucination-driven errors and other orchestration-level malfunctions.

2601.10460.tldr: It is shown that measured bias shifts dramatically when prompts mention different places, times, or audiences -- no adversarial prompting required, and CSF forces evaluators to ask "Under what conditions does bias appear?"rather than "Is this model biased?"

2601.10477.tldr: This work introduces the Urban Socio-Semantic Segmentation dataset named SocioSeg, a new resource comprising satellite imagery, digital maps, and pixel-level labels of social semantic entities organized in a hierarchical structure, and proposes a novel vision-language reasoning framework called SocioReasoner that simulates the human process of identifying and annotating social semantic entities via cross-modal recognition and multi-stage reasoning.

2601.10496.tldr: An exposure-aware evaluation framework that quantifies how prior exposure to buggy versus fixed code influences a model's preference is introduced, indicating that exposure can skew bug-fix evaluations and highlight the risk that LLMs may propagate memorised errors in practice.

2601.10511.tldr: A new Monte Carlo approach with an adaptive stopping rule and short-circuit formula evaluation is developed that achieves Probably Approximately Correct (PAC) learning bounds and is asymptotically more efficient than the previous methods.

2601.10524.tldr: This work introduces and applies a multi-layered diagnostic framework to a cross-architectural study and provides a concrete methodology for diagnosing and understanding generalization failures, underscoring that reliable AI requires deep validation of the interplay between architecture, data, and training strategy.

2601.10560.tldr: This work proposes Latency-Aware Multi-agent System (LAMaS), a latency-aware multi-agent orchestration framework that enables parallel execution and explicitly optimizes the critical execution path, allowing the controller to construct execution topology graphs with lower latency under parallel execution.

2601.10562.tldr: The Process-Guided Concept Bottleneck Model is proposed, an extension of CBMs which constrains learning to follow domain-defined causal mechanisms through biophysically meaningful intermediate concepts and reduces error and bias compared to multiple benchmarks, whilst leveraging multi-source heterogeneous training data and producing interpretable intermediate outputs.

2601.10567.tldr: It is claimed that the distinctive nature of LLMsmotivates the need for an interactionist paradigm consisting of alternative theoretical foundations, methodologies, and analytical tools, in order to systematically examine how prior knowledge and embedded values interact with social context to shape emergent phenomena in multi-agent generative AI systems.

2601.10581.tldr: GenomAgent is proposed, a multi-agent framework that efficiently coordinates specialized agents for complex genomics queries and its flexible architecture extends beyond genomics to various scientific domains needing expert knowledge extraction.

2601.10587.tldr: A white-box attack on computer vision models using SHAP values is introduced to demonstrate how adversarial evasion attacks can compromise the performance of deep learning models by reducing output confidence or inducing misclassifications.

2601.10591.tldr: Evaluation on cryptocurrency return forecasting demonstrates that DER maintains competitive forecasting accuracy while providing explicit epistemic-aleatoric uncertainty decomposition, establishing both an extensible framework for principled uncertainty quantification in foundation models and empirical evidence for DER's effectiveness in financial applications.

2601.10651.tldr: A fully symbolic algorithm is developed that introduces Boolean goal variables and exploits monotonicity to represent exponentially many goal combinations compactly and substantially outperforms enumeration-based baselines.

2601.10679.tldr: Three strategies to scale HRM's guesses are proposed: data augmentation, input perturbation, and model bootstrapping (scaling the number of guesses by leveraging inference randomness), and model bootstrapping (scaling the number of guesses by leveraging training randomness).

2601.10681.tldr: A structure-informed and diversity-constrained context bubble construction framework is proposed that assembles coherent, citable bundles of spans under a strict token budget and significantly reduces redundant context, is better able to cover secondary facets and has a better answer quality and citation faithfulness within a limited context window.

2601.10684.tldr: It is demonstrated that this simplified setting already gives rise to neural scaling laws even in the absence of power law structure in the data correlations, and preliminary evidence that maximal update parameterization may be more parameter efficient than standard parameterization is provided.

2601.10696.tldr: It is suggested that GenAI effectiveness depends on users'prior expertise and interaction strategies through prompting, though prompt usage patterns showed that iterative idea generation and visual feedback prompts were linked to greater reductions in cognitive load.

2601.10702.tldr: STITCH (Structured Intent Tracking in Contextual History), an agentic memory system that indexes each trajectory step with a structured retrieval cue, contextual intent, and retrieves history by matching the current step's intent, substantially reduces retrieval noise.

2601.10712.tldr: This work proposes MatchTIR, a framework that introduces fine-grained supervision via bipartite matching-based turn-level reward assignment and dual-level advantage estimation, and introduces a dual-level advantage estimation scheme that integrates turn-level and trajectory-level signals.

2206.13405.tldr: This work addresses the challenge of evaluating corruption robustness in a way that allows comparability and interpretability on a given dataset, and strengthens the view that a tradeoff between accuracy and corruption robustness is not inherent.

2306.07541.tldr: A simple unified uncertainty-guided (SUNG) framework, which naturally unifies the solution to both challenges with the tool of uncertainty with state-action visitation density estimator, achieves state-of-the-art online finetuning performance when combined with different offline RL methods, across various environments and datasets in the D4RL benchmark.

2309.03773.tldr: This work optimally propagate known embeddings of a subgraph to inductively represent new entities introduced into the knowledge graph at inference time, and shows that on a number of large-scale knowledge graph embedding benchmarks, this method is competitive with -- and in some scenarios outperforms -- more complex models derived explicitly for inductive knowledge graph reasoning tasks.

2406.01423.tldr: This work proposes to decouple the acting policy from the policy evaluated by the critic, which allows the agent to separately improve the critic's policy with greedier updates while maintaining the slow gradient-based improvement to the parameterized acting policy.

2407.05934.tldr: REinforced Graph Anomaly Detector (REGAD) is proposed, which pruning the edges of candidate nodes potentially with mistaken labels by pruning the edges of candidate nodes potentially with mistaken labels to perform effective GAD with noisy labels.

2407.20114.tldr: The FiCo-ITR library is introduced, which standardises evaluation methodologies for both FG and CG models, facilitating direct comparisons and offering new insights into the performance-efficiency trade-offs between recent representative FG and CG models, highlighting their respective strengths and limitations.

2410.07173.tldr: It is found that decoder-based models exhibit stronger visual alignment than encoders, even when controlling for model and dataset size, and language modeling performance correlates with visual generalization, suggesting that advances in unimodal LLMs can simultaneously improve vision models.

2501.01439.tldr: ProMis is an interpretable and adaptable system architecture that links uncertain geospatial data and noisy perception with declarative, Hybrid Probabilistic Logic Programs (HPLP) to reason over the agent’s state space and its legality, and yields Probabilistic Mission Landscapes (PML).

2501.18100.tldr: This work proposes Panacea, which optimizes an adaptive perturbation that will be applied to the model after fine-tuning that maintains model's safety alignment performance without compromising downstream fine-tuning performance.

2502.10803.tldr: This work proposes Post-hoc Distribution Alignment (PDA), a generalized and model-agnostic framework for detecting AI-generated images under unknown generative threats that achieves average detection accuracy of 96.69%, outperforming the best baseline by 10.71%.

2503.15512.tldr: It is suggested that policy and policy enforcement alone are insufficient to produce meaningful end-user explanations and that responsible AI frameworks may overestimate developers'ability to translate high-level requirements into human-centered designs without additional training, tools, or implementation support.

2503.18197.tldr: This work proposes a novel framework that jointly optimizes both the graph structure and the model to achieve fair unlearning, and rewires the graph by removing redundant edges that hinder forgetting while preserving fairness through targeted edge augmentation.

2503.22358.tldr: It is proved that every WSMS measure can be equivalently seen as the Shapley value of a suitably defined cooperative game, and WSMS measures enjoy tractable data complexity for a large class of queries, including all unions of conjunctive queries.

2505.08687.tldr: AC-PKAN is presented, a novel architecture that constitutes an enhancement to weakly supervised Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) and extends the expressive power of KANs and consistently outperforms or matches state-of-the-art models such as PINNsFormer.

2505.11831.tldr: ARC-AGI-2 aims to serve as a next-generation tool for rigorously measuring progress towards more general and human-like AI capabilities, and incorporates a newly curated and expanded set of tasks specifically designed to provide a more granular signal to assess abstract reasoning and problem-solving abilities at higher levels of fluid intelligence.

2505.24149.tldr: Experimental results on four domain generalization datasets demonstrate that the RCCDA policy outperforms baseline methods in inference accuracy while adhering to strict resource constraints under several schedules of concept drift, making the solution uniquely suited for real-time ML deployments.

2506.00070.tldr: This work introduces Robot-R1, a novel framework that leverages reinforcement learning to enhance embodied reasoning specifically for robot control and surpasses GPT-4o on reasoning tasks related to low-level action control, such as spatial and movement reasoning.

2506.01820.tldr: It is claimed that Fodor and Pylyshyn's legacy persists, and to date, there is no human-like systematic compositionality learned in neural networks, and limitations in the proposed meta-learning framework for compositionality are highlighted.

2506.10622.tldr: SDialog, an MIT-licensed open-source Python toolkit that unifies dialog generation, evaluation and mechanistic interpretability into a single end-to-end framework for building and analyzing LLM-based conversational agents, enables researchers to build, benchmark and understand conversational systems more systematically.

2506.11578.tldr: This work proposes COPE, a test-time collaboration framework that achieves performance comparable to large proprietary models, while drastically reducing the inference API cost, and highlights planning as an effective prior for cost-efficient inference.

2506.12537.tldr: This work systematically investigate the role of speech tokenizer designs in LLM-centric SLMs, augmented by speech heads and speaker modeling and proposes a speaker-aware generation paradigm and introduces RoleTriviaQA, a large-scale role-playing knowledge QA benchmark with diverse speaker identities.

2507.03585.tldr: Causal-SAM-LLM establishes a new state of the art in out-of-distribution (OOD) robustness, improving the average Dice score by up to 6.2 points and reducing the Hausdorff Distance by 15.8 mm over the strongest baseline, all while using less than 9% of the full model's trainable parameters.

2507.12979.tldr: This work proposes a novel approach for decentralized GAN training that enables utilizing distributed data and underutilized, low-capability devices while not sharing data in its raw form, combining KLD-weighted Clustered Federated Learning with Heterogeneous U-Shaped split learning to tackle the challenge of device heterogeneity under strict data sharing constraints.

2508.01687.tldr: PHAR--Post-hoc Attribution Rules--a unified framework that transforms numeric feature attributions from post-hoc, instance-wise explainers into structured, human-readable rules that can enhance model transparency by localizing threshold-based conditions on the raw series.
