2601.20856.tldr: This work provides a systematic assessment of the planning and long-horizon reasoning capabilities of state-of-the-art Large Reasoning Models (LRMs), and proposes a novel benchmark based on Sokoban puzzles, revealing a consistent degradation in planning performance when more than 25 moves are required to reach the solution.

2601.20861.tldr: A comprehensive analysis of Evolutionary Strategies is performed and finds that ES is able to reach performance numbers close to GRPO for math and reasoning tasks with a comparable compute budget, but the performance gains are accompanied by significant forgetting of prior abilities, limiting its applicability for training models online.

2309.16117.tldr: Low-redundancy Distillation (LoRD), a novel CL method that enhances model performance while maintaining training efficiency, is proposed by eliminating redundancy in three aspects of CL: student model redundancy, teacher model redundancy, and rehearsal sample redundancy.

2407.21666.tldr: This work proposed an explainable deep learning pipeline that leverages the power of ViTs for drought stress detection in potato crops using aerial imagery using a synergistic combination of ViT and support vector machine (SVM), where ViT extracts intricate spatial features from aerial images, and SVM classifies the crops as stressed or healthy.

2411.13578.tldr: COOD is introduced, a novel zero-shot multi-label OOD detection framework that leverages pre-trained vision-language models, enhancing them with a concept-based label expansion strategy and a new scoring function that significantly outperforms existing approaches.

2502.03287.tldr: STEMS, Spatial-Temporal Mapping for SNNs is introduced and it is shown that neuron states may not be needed in early SNN layers, and energy performance is improved by 1.4x without sacrificing accuracy.

2502.04379.tldr: This paper evaluates comprehensively the capacity of popular LLMs for successfully predicting continuous affect annotations of videos when prompted by a sequence of text and video frames in a multimodal fashion, and suggests they generally fall behind continuous experience annotations provided by humans.

2502.07202.tldr: This paper introduces Monte Carlo Tree Diffusion (MCTD), a novel framework that integrates the generative strength of diffusion models with the adaptive search capabilities of MCTS, allowing partially denoised plans to be iteratively evaluated, pruned, and refined.

2504.06160.tldr: Analysis of a recently released large-scale bias audit dataset reveals that mental health entities occupy central positions within attack narrative networks, as revealed by a significantly higher mean centrality of closeness and dense clustering.

2504.16214.tldr: Hexcute is proposed, a compiler framework that automates layout synthesis while providing explicit control over dataflow and pipelining while providing explicit control over dataflow and pipelining in GPU programs.

2506.00614.tldr: A predictability-aware compression-decompression framework to reduce runtime, decrease communication cost, and maintain prediction accuracy across diverse predictors, using a circular seasonal key matrix with orthogonality to capture underlying time series predictability during compression.

2506.01042.tldr: This work introduces graph probing, a method for uncovering the functional connectivity of LLM neurons and relating it to language generation performance, and identifies default networks and hub neurons in LLMs and provides causal evidence by interventional experiments on multiple benchmarks, showing that LLMs actually exploit these topological information.

2506.19089.tldr: A programmable framework for synthetically generating stories to evaluate the theory of mind (ToM) and world modeling (WM) capabilities of large language models (LLMs) reveals that most models perform better on WM tasks than ToM tasks, and that models tend to perform better reasoning with humans compared to inanimate objects.

2506.20966.tldr: This work delivers both a comprehensive overview of current VLA model post-training methods from a human motor learning perspective and practical insights for VLA model development.

2506.21599.tldr: Refine-POI is proposed, a framework that addresses challenges through topology-aware ID generation and reinforcement fine-tuning, effectively synthesizing the reasoning capabilities of LLMs with the representational fidelity required for accurate and explainable next-POI recommendation.

2507.03779.tldr: This work proposes a novel pre-training strategy for DINOv2 that simultaneously accelerates convergence--and strengthens robustness to common corruptions as a by-product, making large-scale self-supervised foundation modeling more attainable, while opening the door to novel exploration around data curriculum and augmentation as means to improve self-supervised learning models robustness.

2507.04490.tldr: This work proposes a novel framework for CAD, normalcy score (NS), that explicitly models both the aleatoric and epistemic uncertainties, and builds on heteroscedastic Gaussian process regression, providing confidence intervals that reflect the reliability of the anomaly assessment.

2507.06252.tldr: On fake text generation, the work demonstrates how adversarial text generation techniques can create fake cybersecurity and cybersecurity-like text that misleads classifiers, degrades performance, and disrupts system functionality.

2507.13993.tldr: OrthoInsight, a multi-modal deep learning framework for rib fracture diagnosis and report generation, achieves high performance across Diagnostic Accuracy, Content Completeness, Logical Coherence, and Clinical Guidance Value, with an average score of 4.28, outperforming models like GPT-4 and Claude-3.

2507.14516.tldr: The results suggest that structural fidelity in signal representations enhances the semantic representation quality, supporting the consideration of structure-aware metrics as viable alternatives to conventional distance-based methods.

2508.04012.tldr: EMSEdit is proposed, which leverages multi-step backpropagation (MSBP) to effectively capture gradient-activation mapping patterns within editing samples, performs multi-step edits per sample to enhance editing performance under limited data, and introduces norm-based regularization to preserve unedited knowledge while improving training efficiency.

2508.07292.tldr: EndoAgent is proposed, the first memory-guided agent for vision-to-decision endoscopic analysis that integrates iterative reasoning with adaptive tool selection and collaboration and enables sophisticated decision-making by ensuring logical coherence through short-term action tracking and progressively enhancing reasoning acuity through long-term experiential learning.

2508.07452.tldr: This work introduces Stackelberg Coupled Representation and Reinforcement Learning (SCORER), a framework for value-based RL that views representation and Q-learning as two strategic agents in a hierarchical game that leads to a bi-level optimization problem whose solution is approximated by a two-timescale algorithm that creates an asymmetric learning dynamic between the two players.

2508.11667.tldr: Guided Perturbation Sensitivity (GPS), a detection framework that identifies adversarial examples by measuring how embedding representations change when important words are masked, is introduced, providing a practical solution for adversarial text detection.

2508.13421.tldr: It is shown that a domain-agnostic, agentic AI Scientist system can independently navigate the scientific workflow - from hypothesis generation through data collection to manuscript preparation, a step toward embodied AI that can test hypotheses through real-world experiments.

2508.13576.tldr: Simulations show that the AVSE-ECS system with joint training achieves high objective speech intelligibility and improves the signal-to-error ratio by 7.4666 dB compared to the advanced combination encoder strategy.

2508.17850.tldr: This study reveals that high latency significantly increases KL divergence, leading to higher variance of importance weights and training instability, and proposes HeteroRL, a heterogeneous RL architecture that decouples these processes, enabling stable training across geographically distributed nodes connected via the Internet.

2509.01641.tldr: This work proposes a novel diffusion model, termed the non-identical diffusion model, and investigates its application to wireless orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) channel generation, and introduces a matrix that matches the input size to control element-wise noise progression.

2509.03827.tldr: Variation across LLMs in their policy recommendations compared to local experts is revealed, yet potential benefits of the use of LLMs to provide insights for policymaking are suggested, if paired with responsible guardrails, contextual calibrations, and local domain expertise.

2509.11311.tldr: This work introduces *preference reconstruction theory*, a framework that formalizes preference alignment as a representation learning problem: constructing a functional basis of proxy agents and recovering population preferences through weighted aggregation.

2509.15271.tldr: A systematic evaluation of ViT, CLIP, DINOv2, and DINOv3 across a range of mental-rotation tasks finds that self-supervised ViTs capture geometric structure better than supervised ViTs; intermediate layers perform better than final layers; and task difficulty increases with rotation complexity and occlusion, mirroring human reaction times and suggesting similar constraints in embedding space representations.

2509.18874.tldr: These findings provide the first empirical evidence that ad streams serve as a high-fidelity digital footprint, enabling off-platform profiling that inherently bypasses current platform safeguards, highlighting a systemic vulnerability in the ad ecosystem and the urgent need for responsible web AI governance in the generative AI era.

2509.18930.tldr: The GNARL framework is proposed, encompassing the methodology to translate problem formulations from NAR to RL and a learning architecture suitable for a wide range of graph-based problems and, remarkably, applicability even when lacking an expert algorithm.

2509.22161.tldr: A simple and intuitive regularization that achieves more reliable codebook utilization and improves performance compared to prior approaches is introduced.

2509.22740.tldr: Audiovisual instance segmentation requires accurately localizing and tracking sounding objects throughout video sequences and Audio-Centric Query Generation using cross-attention is proposed, enabling each query to selectively attend to distinct sound sources and carry sound-specific priors into visual decoding.

2509.25214.tldr: CoA-LoRA is proposed, a method that dynamically adjusts the LoRA adapter to arbitrary quantization configurations (i.e., the per-layer bit-width choices of a pre-trained model) without requiring repeated fine-tuning without requiring repeated fine-tuning.

2510.03217.tldr: Two complementary LLM-based policies to reduce noise in agentic APR deployment, bug abstention and patch validation, are introduced and provide a practical path to the reliable, industrial-scale deployment of agentic APR systems.

2510.07213.tldr: Experiments on a multilingual generation control task reveal the interpretability of these dimensions, demonstrating that the interventions in these dimensions can switch the output language while preserving semantic content, and that it surpasses the performance of prior neuron-based approaches at a substantially lower cost.

2510.08592.tldr: This work presents a reference-guided diversity reduction protocol (RefDiv) that serves as a diagnostic attack to stress test TTS pipelines, and finds that numerous widely used safety guardrail classifiers are unable to flag the adversarial input prompts generated by RefDiv, demonstrating that existing defenses offer limited protection against this diversity-driven failure mode.

2510.13036.tldr: Preference-Based Reward Repair (PBRR): an automated iterative framework that repairs a human-specified proxy reward function by learning an additive, transition-dependent correction term from preferences that has a cumulative regret that matches, up to constants, that of prior preference-based RL methods.

2510.13244.tldr: Experiments show that MotionBeat outperforms state-of-the-art audio encoders in music-to-dance generation and transfers effectively to beat tracking, music tagging, genre and instrument classification, emotion recognition, and audio-visual retrieval.

2510.13561.tldr: A comprehensive evaluation demonstrates that OpenDerisk significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in both accuracy and efficiency, and is validated by its large-scale production deployment at Ant Group, confirming its industrial-grade scalability and practical impact.

2510.13602.tldr: This work proposes NOSA, a trainable sparse attention mechanism natively designed for KV cache offloading that explicitly constrains the volume of CPU-GPU KV transfers, thereby achieving low communication overhead and high decoding throughput.

2510.14466.tldr: LiRA (Linguistic Robust Anchoring for LLMs)-a plug-and-play framework that requires only lightweight fine-tuning on top of existing pretrained backbones that jointly optimizes representation stability and cross-lingual semantic consistency.

2511.00527.tldr: Experiments on multiple benchmark datasets demonstrate that HIP-LLM offers a more accurate and standardized reliability characterization than existing benchmark and state-of-the-art approaches.

2511.18368.tldr: This work proposes an Intent-Driven Framework for Autonomous Network Optimization comprising prediction and decision modules and introduces Hyperdimensional Transformer (HDT), which embeds data into a Hyperdimensional space via Hyperdimensional vector encoding and replaces standard matrix and attention operations with symbolic Hyperdimensional computations.

2512.02833.tldr: This work empirically establishes REVIN as the most efficient approach, reducing zero-shot MASE by 89\% relative to an un-normalized baseline and by 44\% versus other normalization methods, while matching the best in-domain accuracy without any dataset-level preprocessing -- yielding the highest accuracy-efficiency trade-off.

2512.08147.tldr: The development and evaluation of a scalable back-end system designed for a mobile diabetes prediction application that maintains a failure rate below 5 % and an average latency under 1000 ms, and leverages horizontal scaling, database sharding, and asynchronous communication via a message queue.

2512.21080.tldr: It is shown that making persona benchmarking as decision-relevant as a field experiment is fundamentally a sample-size question, yielding explicit bounds on the number of independent persona evaluations required to reliably distinguish meaningfully different methods at a chosen resolution.

2601.04575.tldr: This work introduces an open recipe for training a video game playing foundation model designed for inference in realtime on a consumer GPU, and observes that the causal improvements seen in the toy domain hold true as model size and training steps increase.

2601.06129.tldr: It is found that only 24.4% of at-risk workers have viable transition pathways and process-oriented skills emerge as the highest-leverage intervention, appearing in 15.6% of pathways.

2601.08360.tldr: HoloMambaRec is presented, a lightweight sequential recommendation architecture that combines holographic reduced representations for attribute-aware embedding with a selective state space encoder for linear-time sequence processing and incorporates forward-compatible mechanisms for temporal bundling and inference-time compression.

2601.09896.tldr: How aesthetic evaluation can perpetuate representational harms and call on AI developers to shift away from prescriptive measures of"aesthetics"toward more pluralistic evaluation is discussed.

2601.11144.tldr: Deep GraphRAG introduces a hierarchical global-to-local retrieval strategy that integrates macroscopic inter-community and microscopic intra-community contextual relations and significantly outperforms baseline graph retrieval methods in both accuracy and efficiency.

2601.11219.tldr: Selective Decoupled Federated LoRA (SDFLoRA), a structure-aware LoRA framework that decouples each client update into a shared component for aggregation and a private component that preserves client-specific semantics, and achieves a strong utility-privacy trade-off.

2601.12247.tldr: This work proposes Plan-Verify-Fill (PVF), a training-free paradigm that grounds planning via quantitative validation and actively constructs a hierarchical skeleton by prioritizing high-leverage semantic anchors and employs a verification protocol to operationalize pragmatic structural stopping where further deliberation yields diminishing returns.

2601.12913.tldr: It is proposed that four symmetries suffice to formalise interpretable models as a subclass of probabilistic models, yield a unified formulation of interpretable inference as a form of Bayesian inversion, and provide a formal framework to verify compliance with safety standards and regulations.

2601.15292.tldr: This research aims to develop a mobile application front-end that presents XAI-driven diabetes risk analysis in an intuitive, understandable format and interprets SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) data into accessible graphical visualizations and narratives.

2601.15930.tldr: This work presents the first systematic study of MM in GR through a contextual lens, and observes that optimal merging weights correlate with context-dependent interaction characteristics, offering practical guidance for weight selection in real-world deployments.

2601.18842.tldr: GUIGuard is proposed, a three-stage framework for privacy-preserving GUI agents: (1) privacy recognition, (2) privacy protection, and (3) task execution under protection.

2601.18987.tldr: Evaluating large language models on a diverse set of C programs from the Termination category of the International Competition on Software Verification 2025 suggests that LLMs perform remarkably well at predicting program termination, where GPT-5 and Claude Sonnet-4.5 would rank just behind the top-ranked tool (using test-time-scaling), and Code World Model (CWM) would place just behind the second-ranked tool.

2601.19092.tldr: A multi-granularity, distribution-aware DSL and compiler that composes thread-local control with collective operators in a single kernel is designed that can bring performance close to hand-tuned kernels on across latest GPU devices and multi-device environments and accelerator backends.

2601.19768.tldr: This paper proposes modeling activations as cognitive elements (CEs), fine-grained, interpretable factors such as''making a threat''and''payment processing'', that can be composed to capture nuanced, domain-specific behaviors with higher precision.

2601.20090.tldr: This work introduces a framework that enables such counterfactual reasoning in agentic LLM-driven control scenarios, while providing formal reliability guarantees, and demonstrates the performance of CCG on a wireless network control use case, demonstrating significant advantages compared to naive re-execution baselines.

2601.20174.tldr: NeuraLSP is articulate, a novel neural preconditioner combined with a novel loss metric that leverages the left singular subspace of the system matrix's near-nullspace vectors that exhibits both theoretical guarantees and empirical robustness to rank inflation.

2601.20176.tldr: This work revisits OOD classification from a causal perspective and proposes to evaluate learned representations based on their necessity and sufficiency under distribution shift, introducing an explicit segment-level framework that directly measures causal effectiveness across domains.

2601.20234.tldr: MALLOC presents a comprehensive investigation and systematic classification of memory management techniques applicable to large sequential recommendations, integrated into state-of-the-art recommenders, enabling a reproducible and accessible evaluation platform.

2601.20335.tldr: The proposed MobileBench-OL is an online benchmark with 1080 tasks from 80 Chinese apps that measures task execution, complex reasoning, and noise robustness of agents by including 5 subsets, which set multiple evaluation dimensions, enabling stable and repeatable real-world benchmarking.

2601.20844.tldr: Study of the minimal dimension required to embed subset memberships into vector spaces, denoted as Minimal Embeddable Dimension (MED), implies that embedding-based retrieval limitations stem primarily from learnability challenges, not geometric constraints, guiding future algorithm design.

2601.20867.tldr: A plug-and-play framework that explicitly regularizes the prompt embedding space by incorporating semantic neighbors generated by large language models, and introduces a novel semantic expansion loss with margin constraints that promote intra-class compactness and inter-class separability, thereby enhancing the semantic structure of the prompt embedding space.

2601.20868.tldr: DASH is a framework that co-optimizes solver search mechanisms and runtime schedules guided by a convergence-aware metric, thereby identifying efficient and high-performance solvers and reducing LLM adaptation costs by about 90%.

2601.20869.tldr: The findings demonstrate that the number of colors in lesions is a significant feature for describing skin conditions, and the proposed CNN, particularly with three skip connections, shows strong potential for clinical application in diagnosing melanoma, supporting its use alongside traditional diagnostic methods.

2601.20870.tldr: STAER is introduced, a novel framework that explicitly preserves temporal structure to bridge the performance gap between SNNs and ANNs and achieves state-of-the-art performance on Sequential-MNIST and Sequential-CIFAR10.

2601.20882.tldr: DevOps-Gym is introduced, the first end-to-end benchmark for evaluating AI agents across core DevOps workflows: build and configuration, monitoring, issue resolving, and test generation, and a semi-automated data collection mechanism with rigorous and non-trivial expert efforts in ensuring the task coverage and quality.

2601.20884.tldr: Finetune-Informed Pretraining (FIP) is proposed, a model-agnostic method that biases representation learning toward a designated target modality needed at fine-tuning time and is simple to implement, architecture-compatible, and broadly applicable across multimodal masked modeling pipelines.

2601.20903.tldr: The Intent-Context Coupling phenomenon is characterized, revealing that LLM safety constraints are significantly relaxed when a malicious intent is coupled with a semantically congruent context pattern and preventing the attack from stagnating in ineffective contexts.

2601.20905.tldr: This work proposes a physics-informed cascade Unet that separates denoising and baseline correction tasks using a new, deterministic Physics Bridge and shows that the cascade architecture eliminates spectral hallucinations found in standard deep learning.

2601.20911.tldr: This work formalizes and target the more challenging non-Markov setting, where a user may refer back to earlier states, undo changes, or reference entities introduced several rounds ago, and demonstrates that explicitly training for non-Markov interactions yields substantial improvements in multi-round consistency and instruction compliance, while maintaining strong single-round editing and personalization.

2601.20913.tldr: This work provides the first systematic treatment of the imperfect-judge setting, yielding interpretable diagnostics of judge reliability and clarifying how evaluation power depends on judge quality, dataset size, and certification levels.

2601.20920.tldr: This work provides the first comprehensive analysis of LLM use across the peer review pipeline, with particular attention to interaction effects: not just whether LLM-assisted papers or LLM-assisted reviews are different in isolation, but whether LLM-assisted reviews evaluate LLM-assisted papers differently.

2601.20994.tldr: This work finds that optimal depth scales as D* ~ C^0.12 while optimal width scales as W* ~ C^0.34, meaning width should grow 2.8x faster than depth, and discovers a critical depth phenomenon: beyond D_crit ~ W^0.44 (sublinear in W), adding layers increases loss despite adding parameters--the Depth Delusion.

2601.21000.tldr: It is found that multi-step and symbolic reasoning tasks pose significant challenges in Urdu, and that stable language alignment is a critical prerequisite for robust reasoning.

2601.21003.tldr: This work reformulates the deterministic LoRA update as a probabilistic low-rank representation inspired by Sparse Gaussian Processes, and identifies a structural isomorphism between LoRA's factorization and Kronecker-factored SGP posteriors, and shows that LoRA emerges as a limiting case when posterior uncertainty collapses.

2601.21016.tldr: Artificial Intelligence is at best a functional mimic, not a conscious experiencing subject, and Biological Idealism is introduced, a framework that-unlike physicalism-remains logically coherent and empirically consistent.

2601.21021.tldr: The Conditional Denoising Model is introduced, a generative model designed to learn the geometry of the physical manifold itself by training the network to restore clean states from noisy ones, and demonstrates that the denoising objective acts as a powerful implicit regularizer.

2601.21028.tldr: An in-depth study to understand what AIG-SC creators make, along with how and why they make it, to inform effective governance in this space.

2601.21031.tldr: A Statistical-prior Informed Generative Masking Architecture (SIGMA-PPG), a generative foundation model featuring a Prior-Guided Adversarial Masking mechanism, where a reinforcement learning-driven teacher leverages statistical priors to create challenging learning paths that prevent overfitting to noise.

2601.21037.tldr: It is suggested that video generation is not merely a media tool, but a scalable, generalizable paradigm for visual reasoning, positing that generated frames can act as intermediate reasoning steps between initial states and solutions.

2601.21049.tldr: These results demonstrate that modeling query uncertainty through recovery hypotheses, coupled with principled anchored aggregation, is essential for robust retrieval under non-faithful queries.

2601.21050.tldr: This work proposes SMKC, a framework that decouples the dynamic input structure from the anomaly detector, and reveals that robust log-distance channels provide the primary discriminative signal, whereas cosine representations often fail to capture sufficient contrast.

2601.21051.tldr: Evaluation across 10 cybersecurity benchmarks and 10 general-purpose benchmarks demonstrates performance competitive with significantly larger models on cybersecurity tasks while maintaining strong general capabilities.

2601.21070.tldr: BEHELM is introduced, a holistic benchmarking infrastructure that unifies software-scenario specification with multi-metric evaluation and provides a structured way to assess models across tasks, languages, input and output granularities, and key quality dimensions.

2601.21076.tldr: This work uses a conditional denoising diffusion probabilistic model to impute missing DWI scans from T1 scans to evaluate whether such imputation improves the accuracy of uni-modal and bi-modal deep learning models for 3-way Alzheimer's disease classification-cognitively normal, mild cognitive impairment, and Alzheimer's disease.

2601.21082.tldr: LOCUS is an attention-based approach that generates embeddings by a deterministic forward pass over query encodings and evaluation scores via an encoder model, enabling seamless incorporation of new models to the pool and refinement of existing model embeddings without having to perform any retraining.

2601.21090.tldr: RL-based adaptive policies are established as a practical solution that bridges the gap between greedy's efficiency and Dijkstra's optimality, providing robust, self-healing communication in fault-prone interconnection networks without requiring the global topology knowledge or computational overhead of optimal algorithms.

2601.21094.tldr: It is demonstrated that test-time shielding, which filters unsafe actions using learned dynamics models, effectively restores safety across algorithms and patient populations, and achieves Time-in-Range gains of 13--14\% for strong baselines such as PPO-Lag and CPO while reducing clinical risk index and glucose variability.

2601.21095.tldr: The Paradox-based Responsible AI Governance (PRAIG) framework is developed, conceptualizing responsible AI governance as the dynamic management of paradoxical tensions between value creation and risk mitigation and provides actionable guidance for developing governance structures that neither stifle innovation nor expose organizations to unacceptable risks.

2601.21096.tldr: Magellan is an agentic framework that evolves the compiler pass itself by synthesizing executable C++ decision logic, producing compact heuristics that integrate directly into existing compilers.

2601.21105.tldr: SteerEval is introduced, an evaluation framework designed to measure more nuanced and diverse forms of steerability by using interventions that range from genres to content-warning for movies.

2601.21113.tldr: A self-improving, cache-optional Planner-Auditor framework that improves safety and reliability by decoupling generation from deterministic validation and targeted replay for high-confidence, low-coverage cases is introduced.

2601.21115.tldr: This work conducts extensive experiments across two model families at two scales (2B and 7B parameters), fine-tuning them for code generation and code summarization tasks, suggesting that careful merging and mixing strategies can effectively combine task-specific capabilities without significant performance degradation, making them ideal for resource-constrained deployment scenarios.

2601.21116.tldr: This position paper argues that AI-assisted software engineering requires explicit mechanisms for tracking the epistemic status and temporal validity of architectural decisions, and formalizes these requirements as the First Principles Framework (FPF), ground its aggregation semantics in fuzzy logic, and define a quintet of invariants that any valid aggregation operator must satisfy.

2601.21128.tldr: This work investigates the use of Large Language Models to automatically generate paraphrased variants of written-language translations as synthetic alternative references for SLT, and introduces BLEUpara, an extension of BLEU that evaluates translations against multiple paraphrased references.

2601.21141.tldr: AnthropoCam is presented, a mobile-based neural style transfer (NST) system optimized for the visual synthesis of Anthropocene environments that reframes neural style transfer as a practical and expressive tool for real-time environmental visualization in the Anthropocene.

2601.21148.tldr: The results establish BrainStack as a functionally modular, neuro-inspired MoE paradigm that unifies neuroscientific priors with adaptive expert routing, paving the way for scalable and interpretable brain-language decoding.

2601.21149.tldr: This work introduces Mobility-Embedded POIs (ME-POIs), a framework that augments POI embeddings derived, from language models with large-scale human mobility data to learn POI-centric, context-independent representations grounded in real-world usage.

2601.21150.tldr: The results suggest that in some cases the representations of even small neural networks can be used to distill interesting abstract structure from new mathematical objects.

2601.21157.tldr: The Cognitive Complexity Benchmark is introduced, a robust evaluation framework grounded in a dataset constructed from 95 real-world Chinese A-share annual reports, providing a transferable architectural insight for precision-critical domains that require tight alignment between semantic understanding and quantitative computation.

2601.21162.tldr: A2RAG couples an adaptive controller that verifies evidence sufficiency and triggers targeted refinement only when necessary, with an agentic retriever that progressively escalates retrieval effort and maps graph signals back to provenance text to remain robust under extraction loss and incomplete graphs.

2601.21165.tldr: FrontierScience is introduced, a benchmark evaluating expert-level scientific reasoning in frontier language models and a granular rubric-based evaluation framework to assess model capabilities throughout the process of solving a research task, rather than judging only a standalone final answer.

2601.21169.tldr: Output-Space Search (OS-Search), which turns LLM generation into endpoint search and Bayesian optimization over Z (code) improves an objective withheld from the controller under matched inference budgets while preserving validity.

2601.21171.tldr: This work proposes AC2L-GAD, an Active Counterfactual Contrastive Learning framework that addresses both limitations of existing methods through principled counterfactual reasoning, and reduces computational overhead by approximately 65% compared to full-graph counterfactual generation while maintaining detection quality.

2601.21181.tldr: This work proposes Modality-Adaptive Decoding (MAD), a training-free method that adaptively weights modality-specific decoding branches based on task requirements based on task requirements, demonstrating that explicit modality awareness through self-assessment is crucial for robust multimodal reasoning.

2601.21182.tldr: This work proposes a flow-matching-based flow-matching-based bi-stage Flow Refinement framework with two refinement strategies operating at different stages: latent space alignment for approximately invertible generators and data space refinement trained with lightweight augmentations.

2601.21189.tldr: The results show that robust aggregation improves consensus alignment with the ground truth proxy and reduces sensitivity to noisy and strategic attacks compared with simple averaging, which motivate robust consensus as a default component for cost-aware Proof of Quality.

2601.21191.tldr: This paper uses cross-linguistic corpus analysis and counterfactual language modeling and ablation experiments to show that language variants preserving all three properties are more easily acquired by neural learners, with frequency and structural association contributing more strongly than boundary alignment.

2601.21192.tldr: Empirically, the findings suggest that unlike Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT), RLVR optimizes trajectories within an existing semantic landscape rather than fundamentally restructuring the landscape itself.

2601.21198.tldr: This paper implements a prototype of ZipMoE, an efficient and semantically lossless on-device MoE serving system that exploits the synergy between the hardware properties of edge devices and the statistical redundancy inherent to MoE parameters via a caching-scheduling co-design with provable performance guarantee.

2601.21199.tldr: This work proposes Thinker, a large vision-language foundation model designed for embodied intelligence, and introduces a simple yet effective approach that substantially enhances the model's capacity for video comprehension by jointly incorporating key frames and full video sequences as inputs.

2601.21207.tldr: A cellular sheaf theoretic framework for modeling and analyzing the local consistency and harmonicity of node features and edge weights in graph-based architectures is introduced, and a multiscale extension inspired by topological data analysis (TDA) is proposed to capture hierarchical feature interactions in graph models.

2601.21208.tldr: This work proposes a novel RL framework called Adaptive Complex Query Optimization (ACQO), designed to adaptively determine when and how to expand the search process, and adopt a Curriculum Reinforcement Learning (CRL) approach, which stabilizes the training process by progressively introducing more challenging queries through a two-stage strategy.

2601.21210.tldr: DoVerifier is proposed, a simple symbolic verifier that checks whether LLM-generated causal expressions are derivable from a given causal graph using rules from do-calculus and probability theory, offering a more rigorous and informative way to evaluate LLMs on causal reasoning.

2601.21212.tldr: Experimental validation across diverse urban settings shows that Intelli-Planner surpasses traditional baselines and achieves comparable performance to state-of-the-art DRL-based methods in objective metrics, while enhancing stakeholder satisfaction and convergence speed.

2601.21215.tldr: A practical efficiency-robustness trade-off is revealed: S5 for parameter-efficient peak accuracy; EEGXF when robustness and conservative uncertainty are critical; EEGXF when robustness and conservative uncertainty are critical.

2601.21221.tldr: This work proposes a dual-encoding causal discovery approach that addresses limitations by running constraint-based algorithms with complementary encoding strategies and merging results through majority voting to identify causal structures that align with established explainable methods.

2601.21225.tldr: Evaluations across nine languages reveal that many low-resource languages suffer large performance drops when tested on digit instantiations different from those in the original test set, and it is found that some proprietary models are less robust to digit instantiation, whereas Claude 4.0 Sonnet is more robust.

2601.21226.tldr: This paper argues that static, compliance-based governance fails once decision-making moves to runtime and becomes opaque, and position runtime governance, specifically, a newly proposed concept called the Governance Twin; as a strong candidate for preserving human relevance, while acknowledging that accountability, agency, and even punishment must be rethought in this transition.

2601.21235.tldr: Application of SHARP to eleven frontier LLMs reveals that models with similar average risk can exhibit more than twofold differences in tail exposure and volatility, indicating that responsible evaluation and governance of LLMs require moving beyond scalar averages toward multidimensional, tail-sensitive risk profiling.

2601.21238.tldr: PTQ4ARVG, a training-free post-training quantization (PTQ) framework consisting of a Gain-Projected Scaling (GPS), Static Token-Wise Quantization (STWQ) and Distribution-Guided Calibration (DGC) that selects samples that contribute most to distributional entropy, eliminating the sample-wise distribution mismatch.

2601.21242.tldr: This paper constructs a SignReLU-based neural estimator for the reverse process and derive bounds on the excess Kullback-Leibler (KL) risk between the generated and true data distributions, and provides generalization guarantees for finite-sample training of diffusion-based generative models.

2601.21246.tldr: This paper proposes an artificial intelligence discrimination framework based on a peak-aware conditional generative model to improve the reliability of GC-MS measurements under interference conditions and verifies how the generative model improves the performance of the AI discrimination framework.

2601.21249.tldr: It is argued that the plasticity-stability paradox cannot be fully resolved by global parameter updates (whether via offline fine-tuning or online adaptation), and advocated a Modular Sovereignty paradigm, which ensures regime-conditional validity, rigorous disentanglement of aleatoric and epistemic uncertainties, and modular auditability.

2601.21255.tldr: This work operationalizes Hypersolid, a method using short-range hard-ball repulsion to prevent local collisions to result in a high-separation geometric regime that preserves augmentation diversity, excelling on fine-grained and low-resolution classification tasks.

2601.21269.tldr: This work proposes a lightweight, high-fidelity, low-bitrate 3D talking face compression framework that integrates FLAME-based parametric modeling with 3DGS neural rendering, and introduces a compact representation and compression scheme, including Gaussian attribute compression and MLP optimization, to enhance transmission efficiency.

2601.21276.tldr: Evaluation results indicate that LLM Agents frequently disregard code reuse opportunities, resulting in higher levels of redundancy compared to human developers, suggesting that the surface-level plausibility of AI code masks redundancy, leading to the silent accumulation of technical debt in real-world development environments.

2601.21278.tldr: The first benchmark for geolocation reasoning chains is introduced and reveals that while large, closed-source VLMs such as Gemini and GPT 5 rival human experts at prediction locations, they still lag behind human experts when it comes to producing auditable reasoning chains.

2601.21283.tldr: Examination of existing benchmarks with enriched evaluation protocols demonstrate that DUET achieves higher performance in both forgetting and utility preservation, while being orders of magnitude more data-efficient than state-of-the-art unlearning methods.

2601.21284.tldr: This paper proposes Physics-Informed Learning via Diffusion (PILD), a framework that unifies diffusion modeling and first-principles physical constraints by introducing a virtual residual observation sampled from a Laplace distribution to supervise generation during training.

2601.21288.tldr: Drive-KD is proposed, a framework that decomposes autonomous driving into a perception-reasoning-planningriad and transfers these capabilities via knowledge distillation via layer-specific attention as the distillation signal to construct capability-specific single-teacher models that outperform baselines.

2601.21293.tldr: The Physics-Guided Tiny-Mamba Transformer (PG-TMT), a compact tri-branch encoder tailored for online condition monitoring, coupling physics-aligned representations with EVT-calibrated decision rules, delivers calibrated, interpretable, and deployment-ready early warnings for reliability-centric prognostics and health management.

2601.21306.tldr: Surprisingly, it is found that search can harm performance even when the model is highly accurate, and it is shown that mitigating distribution shift matters more than improving model or value function accuracy.

2601.21316.tldr: A unified optimization model that integrates strategy selection for both air and ground transportation and leverages deep reinforcement learning and Vehicle-to-Everything communication to optimize vertiport selection and dynamically plan air taxi routes is proposed.

2601.21321.tldr: Experiments show that, unlike the uninterpretable black-box baseline which finally fails in 5 topologies, White-Op achieves reliable, interpretable behavioral-level designs with only 8.52\% theoretical prediction error and the design functionality retains after transistor-level mapping for all topologies.

2601.21323.tldr: It is demonstrated that adversarial vulnerability is not an artifact of end-to-end differentiability but a fundamental property of image classification systems, with implications for security-critical deployments across computational paradigms.

2601.21335.tldr: This work proposes a novel Causal Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning model for Explainable Multi-Behavior Recommendation (CNRE), which operationalizes the endogenous logic by simulating a human-like decision-making process and generates an explainable causal mediator that approximates an ideal state isolated from confounding effects.

2601.21339.tldr: Inspiration prompts are powerful levers for steering output quality, but given the substantial within-LLM variance, single-sample evaluations risk conflating sampling noise with genuine prompt or model effects.

2601.21340.tldr: Experiments show that EHR-RAG consistently outperforms the strongest LLM-based baselines, achieving an average Macro-F1 improvement of 10.76%.

2601.21342.tldr: Ostrakon-VL, an FSRS-oriented MLLM based on Qwen3-VL-8B, and QUAD (Quality-aware Unbiased Automated Data-curation), a multi-stage multimodal instruction data curation pipeline are developed, establishing a new state of the art among open-source MLLMs with comparable parameter scales and diverse architectures.

2601.21344.tldr: This work establishes a strong foundation for next-generation AI-driven educational tools, advancing equitable and impactful learning outcomes by addressing limitations in static moderation and personalization in existing systems.

2601.21348.tldr: Experiments demonstrate that shifting learning emphasis toward later denoising steps consistently reduces memorization and improves distributional alignment with training data, validating the generality and effectiveness of the proposed timestep sampling strategy.

2601.21349.tldr: This work proposes Low-rank Lipschitz-controlled Routing (L2R), a unified routing framework that reshapes both the routing space and scoring geometry and incorporates a parameter-efficient multi-anchor routing mechanism to enhance expert expressiveness.

2601.21351.tldr: This work develops a tractable analytical framework for sizing AFD bundles in an $r$A-$1$F topology, where the key difficulty is that Attention-side work is nonstationary-token context grows and requests are continuously replenished with random lengths-while FFN work is stable given the aggregated batch.

2601.21352.tldr: This work model GUI task execution as a DFS process and proposes BEAP-Agent, a DFS-based framework that supports long-range, multi-level state backtracking with dynamic task tracking and updating and validating the effectiveness of the proposed method.

2601.21360.tldr: The findings suggest that current alignment paradigms create a "Trojan" vulnerability in automated grading, necessitating a shift from standard RLHF toward domain-specific Adjudicative Robustness, where models are conditioned to prioritize evidence over instruction compliance.

2601.21367.tldr: A novel model-agnostic Global-guided Hebbian Learning (GHL) framework, which seamlessly integrates local and global information to scale up across diverse networks and tasks, and significantly narrows the gap with standard backpropagation.

2601.21372.tldr: NEMO is a system that translates Natural-language descriptions of decision problems into formal Executable Mathematical Optimization implementations, operating collaboratively with users or autonomously, demonstrating the power of execution-aware agentic architectures for automated optimization modeling.

2601.21375.tldr: A syllabus-grounded evaluation framework that measures LLM teaching capability via student performance improvement after multi-turn instruction and highlights teaching ability as a distinct and measurable dimension of LLM behavior is proposed.

2601.21384.tldr: Sim-MSTNet is proposed, a multi-task spatiotemporal network traffic forecasting model based on the sim2real approach that reduces the distributional gap between synthetic and real data through bi-level optimization of both sample weighting and model training and applies dynamic loss weighting to balance task objectives.

2601.21386.tldr: While FSD and SMMD cannot fully replace subjective evaluation, they can serve as complementary, cost-efficient, and reproducible measures, particularly useful when large-scale or direct listening assessments are infeasible.

2601.21391.tldr: This work proposes a policy optimization framework that leverages multiple intrinsic rewards to directly optimize a policy for an extrinsic reward without pretraining subpolicies and achieves this by using a surrogate policy gradient that provides a more informative learning signal than the true gradient in sparse-reward environments.

2601.21403.tldr: DataCross, a novel benchmark and collaborative agent framework for unified, insight-driven analysis across heterogeneous data modalities, and the DataCrossAgent framework, inspired by the "divide-and-conquer" workflow of human analysts are proposed.

1810.06284.tldr: CURIOUS is proposed, an algorithm that leverages a modular Universal Value Function Approximator with hindsight learning to achieve a diversity of goals of different kinds within a unique policy and an automated curriculum learning mechanism that biases the attention of the agent towards goals maximizing the absolute learning progress.

2407.04503.tldr: By tracking the evolution of text toxicity, positivity, difficulty, and length across transmission chains, the existence of biases and attractors are uncovered, and their dependence on the initial text, the instructions, language model, and model size is studied.

2409.13959.tldr: This paper formally introduces and study two query answering problems, namely, query answer classification and query answer retrieval, and proposes AnyCQ, a model that can classify answers to any conjunctive query on any knowledge graph.

2409.14038.tldr: The OAEI-LLM dataset is an extended version of the Ontology Alignment Evaluation Initiative (OAEI) datasets that evaluate LLM-specific hallucinations in OM tasks and outlines the methodology used in dataset construction and schema extension.

2410.00564.tldr: This paper introduces JOWA: Jointly-Optimized World-Action model, an offline model-based RL agent pretrained on multiple Atari games with 6 billion tokens data to learn general-purpose representation and decision-making ability and proposes a provably efficient and parallelizable planning algorithm to compensate for the Q-value estimation error.

2410.01308.tldr: An alternative framework for studying GNN expressivity based on an extended CONGEST model with an explicit preprocessing phase is proposed, identifying implicit shortcuts introduced in prior analyses and establishing further results for WL tests in settings where graphs are augmented with virtual nodes and virtual edges.

2410.04328.tldr: This work considers coverless steganography where a Large Language Model is used to generate stego-texts in combination with arithmetic coding and shows that this problem is equivalent to maximizing the entropy of a replacement probability distribution of the next token generation, subject to a constraint on the divergence between the new distribution and the original one produced by the LLM.

2410.12481.tldr: This paper presents and studies an adaptation of Soft Actor-Critic and hindsight relabeling to LLM agents that not only paves the path towards autotelic LLM agents that learn online but can also outperform on-policy methods in more classic multi-goal RL environments.

2411.02168.tldr: This paper presents a model agnostic explainability pipeline for Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) employing diagnostic classifiers and proposes to consider graph-theoretic properties as the features of choice for studying the emergence of representations in GNNs.

2411.07042.tldr: This paper examines how users negotiate such harmful conflicts with AI companions and what emotional and practical burdens are created when mitigation is pushed to user-side tools, and introduces Minion, a Chrome-based technology probe that offers candidate responses spanning persuasion, rational appeals, boundary setting, and appeals to platform rules.

2412.03671.tldr: This paper extends the Repeated Risk Minimization framework by utilizing historical datasets from previous retraining snapshots, yielding a class of algorithms that are called Affine Risk Minimizers and enabling convergence to a performatively stable point for a broader class of problems.

2501.17377.tldr: This work introduces a two-phase training framework enhanced by Model-Agnostic Meta-Learning (MAML) to prime the model for fast adaptation and demonstrates that ASAP improves the generalization capability of state-of-the-art baselines and achieves superior online adaptation on out-of-distribution instances.

2503.04796.tldr: This paper identifies a three-stage information processing pattern in LLMs during layer-by-layer reasoning, consisting of extraction, processing, and subsequent extraction steps, which suggests that the representations in intermediate layers contain richer information compared to those in other layers.

2504.02492.tldr: This paper models a differential-drive robot with nonholonomic constraints, then decomposes motion into obstacle avoidance, target turning, and target approaching behaviors to parameterize the control variables and improves robustness of global navigation in practice.

2505.00570.tldr: Extensive experiments demonstrate that FreqKV enables robust context window extension and consistently outperforms existing KV cache compression methods on LLaMA-2 and LLaMA-3, highlighting its effectiveness for both understanding and generation in long contexts.

2505.05029.tldr: RepuNet is proposed, a dynamic, dual-level reputation framework that models both agent-level reputation dynamics and system-level network evolution and finds that reputation systems can give rise to rich emergent behaviors in LLM-based MASs, such as the formation of cooperative clusters, the social isolation of exploitative agents, and the preference for sharing positive gossip rather than negative ones.

2505.11766.tldr: An auxiliary dimension is introduced that explicitly models embedding evolution in operator form, thereby redefining the NO framework in d+1 dimensions (the original $d$ dimensions plus one auxiliary dimension), and developing a Schrodingerised Kernel Neural Operator (SKNO), which leverages Fourier-based operators to model the dimensional evolution.

2505.15998.tldr: Though demonstrated specifically with Flow-Lenia, this methodology provides a framework potentially applicable to other parameterizable complex systems where understanding emergent collective properties is of interest, and provides a framework potentially applicable to other parameterizable complex systems where understanding emergent collective properties is of interest.

2505.19616.tldr: A unified finetuning framework is proposed that combines heuristic and adversarial perturbation-based data augmentation with output-level consistency regularization between original and perturbed inputs.

2505.21627.tldr: This work develops an efficient heuristic algorithm that allows providers to significantly overcharge users without raising suspicion, and demonstrates that the cost of running the algorithm is lower than the additional revenue from overcharging users, highlighting the vulnerability of users under the current pay-per-token pricing mechanism.

2506.00660.tldr: This scoping review synthesizes applications of DP in medical DL across centralized and federated settings and identifies key gaps in fairness auditing and standardization, and outlines priorities for equitable, clinically robust privacy-preserving DL.

2506.00886.tldr: The Theory of Agent is introduced, a framework that treats agents as making sequential decisions about whether remaining uncertainty should be resolved internally or delegated externally, and provides a normative criterion for tool use that complements existing decision-theoretic models and is essential for building agents that are not only correct, but increasingly intelligent.

2506.01883.tldr: This work presents scDataset, a PyTorch data loader that enables efficient training from on-disk data with seamless integration across diverse storage formats and empirically shows that scDataset matches the performance of true random sampling across multiple classification tasks.

2506.03229.tldr: This paper jointly train two neural networks to perform collaborative label purification via a co-pseudo-labeling mechanism, while enforcing consistency regularization in both label and feature representation spaces and proposes a collaborative consistency regularization (Co-Reg) framework.

2506.06725.tldr: WorldLLM is presented, a framework that enhances LLM-based world modeling by combining Bayesian inference and autonomous active exploration with reinforcement learning and generates human-interpretable theories of environment dynamics.

2506.11860.tldr: MindGrab is a lightweight, fully convolutional model for volumetric skull stripping across all imaging modalities that demonstrates state-of-the-art performance, with up to 40-fold speedups and substantially lower memory demands compared to established methods.

2506.17254.tldr: StageRoute is introduced, a hierarchical algorithm that optimistically selects up to $M_{\max}$ models for the next stage using reward upper-confidence and cost lower-confidence bounds, and routes each incoming query by solving a budget- and throughput-constrained bandit subproblem over the deployed set.

2506.17357.tldr: An original tensor-based GPU acceleration method designed to speed up the commonly used local search operators in vehicle routing by using an attribute-based representation, which offers broad extensibility, making it applicable to different VRP variants.

2507.15465.tldr: This paper argues that recent architectural advances in transformer models -- Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA) and Mixture of Experts (MoE) -- introduce new dominant bottlenecks, shifting the challenge away from memory-intensive attention and towards a compute-bound regime well-matched to modern accelerators such as GPUs.

2508.13187.tldr: A type of ostracism that directly impacts poverty-reduction policymaking is uncovered, enabling low-cost, privacy-preserving deployment without relying on commercial APIs.

2508.21172.tldr: It is shown that leveraging a hierarchy of untrained residual recurrent layers significantly boosts memory capacity and long-term temporal modeling within Deep Residual Echo State Networks (DeepResESNs).

2509.00190.tldr: This paper introduces a state-aware transition framework that abstracts CoT trajectories into structured latent dynamics and model their progression as a Markov chain, yielding a structured and interpretable view of the reasoning process.

2509.04154.tldr: RFA is introduced, an attention mechanism that reformulates self-attention as parallel robust filtering under a latent stochastic differential equation (SDE) prior, where analytically propagated uncertainty defines a time-dependent precision prior over attention weights.

2509.12991.tldr: A simple yet effective post-training approach to enhance ECG foundation models, which demonstrates improved training dynamics and data efficiency and underscores the potential of post-training strategies to improve ECG foundation models.

2509.17866.tldr: A systematic singular value decomposition (SVD) analysis of principal linear layers in pretrained LLMs, focusing on two widely adopted post-training methods: instruction tuning and long-chain-of-thought (Long-CoT) distillation, reveals two unexpected and robust structural changes.

2509.18531.tldr: This work proposes an iterative Direct Preference Optimization scheme that attains the highest human preference (ELO) with competitive CER, outperforming GRPO and strong commercial baselines and suggests that when prosody cannot be rewarded automatically, this scheme offers a practical and data-efficient path to natural and robust TTS.

2509.20912.tldr: DeFacto, a counterfactual reasoning framework that jointly enforces accurate answering and faithful reasoning, is proposed and trained with GRPO-based reinforcement learning, where three complementary rewards are designed to guide the model toward accurate answering and evidence-grounded reasoning.

2509.22259.tldr: It is found that rotating tokens depending on the spectrum of the graph Laplacian efficiently injects structural information into the attention mechanism, boosting performance in synthetic and real-world graph learning tasks.

2509.23019.tldr: This work theoretically analyzed rewriting-based evasion, demonstrating that reducing the average conditional probability of sampling green tokens by a small margin causes the detection probability to decay exponentially, and proposes the Bias-Inversion Rewriting Attack (BIRA), a practical query-free method that applies a negative logit bias to a proxy suppression set identified via token surprisal.

2509.23694.tldr: This work proposes SafeSearch, an automated red-teaming framework that is scalable, cost-efficient, and lightweight, enabling harmless safety evaluation of search agents, and reveals substantial vulnerabilities in LLM-based search agents.

2509.25239.tldr: A formal analysis is presented showing that latent thought admits more efficient parallel computation than inherently sequential CoT, and suggesting the tasks for which depth-driven recursion is more suitable, thereby offering practical guidance for choosing between reasoning paradigms.

2509.26157.tldr: Extensive experiments on long-term forecasting, classification, and anomaly detection demonstrate that the proposed Entropy-Guided Dynamic Patch Encoder improves both accuracy and efficiency, establishing entropy-guided dynamic patching as a promising new paradigm for time series modeling.

2510.02190.tldr: Dr. Bench is introduced, a multidimensional evaluation framework tailored to DRAs and long-form report-style responses that provides a robust foundation for capability assessment, architectural refinement, and paradigm advancement of DRAs.

2510.02422.tldr: Dynamic Target Attack (DTA), which leverages the target LLM's own responses as adaptive targets, achieves over 87% average attack success rate (ASR) within 200 optimization iterations on recent safety-aligned LLMs, exceeding the state-of-the-art baselines by over 15% and reducing wall-clock time by 2-26x.

2510.02999.tldr: This work proposes the first gradient-based untargeted jailbreak attack (UJA), which relies on an untargeted objective to maximize the unsafety probability of the LLM output, without enforcing any response patterns.

2510.16797.tldr: This work introduces MOSAIC (Masked Objective with Selective Adaptation for In-domain Contrastive learning), a multi-stage framework for domain adaptation of text embedding models that incorporates joint domain-specific masked supervision and demonstrates the effectiveness of each component.

2510.25262.tldr: IB-Inspired Normalization (IBNorm), a simple yet powerful family of methods grounded in the Information Bottleneck principle, is proposed, which introduces bounded compression operations that encourage embeddings to preserve predictive information while suppressing nuisance variability, yielding more informative representations while retaining the stability and compatibility of standard normalization.

2511.05759.tldr: There is a clear gap between the theoretical possibility of language generation in the limit and its computational feasibility, and infeasibility already appears for context-free and regular languages, and persists even for strict subclasses such as locally threshold testable languages.

2511.06411.tldr: A novel policy optimization algorithm, SofT-GRPO, to reinforce LLMs under the soft-thinking reasoning pattern, and demonstrates that SofT-GRPO enables soft-thinking LLMs to slightly outperform discrete-token GRPO on Pass@1 (+0.13% on average accuracy), while exhibiting a substantial uplift on Pass@32 (+2.19% on average accuracy).

2511.07110.tldr: Cooperative Market Making is proposed, a novel framework that decouples LLM features across three orthogonal dimensions: layer, task, and data, and introduces an H\'a}jek-MoE to integrate the output of the student models by investigating the contribution of different models in a kernel function-generated common feature space.

2511.08234.tldr: Geometric Action Control (GAC) is proposed, a novel action generation paradigm that preserves the geometric benefits of spherical distributions while simplifying computation, and suggests that robust and efficient continuous control does not require complex distributions, but a principled respect for the geometry of action spaces.

2511.10233.tldr: EvoReal is presented, which leverages an evolutionary module guided by large language models to generate synthetic instances characterized by diverse and realistic structural patterns, and markedly improves the generalization capabilities of state-of-the-art neural solvers.

2511.16147.tldr: This paper proposes TS-PEFT, a theoretical framework utilizing proximal optimization that acts as a dynamic probe to identify token-level redundancy during the fine-tuning process, and shows that the learned token-level sparsity is a superior indicator of module importance compared to traditional weight criteria.

2511.20002.tldr: The Semantic-Aware Universal Perturbation (SAUP) is introduced, which acts as a semantic router,"actively"perceiving input semantics and routing them to distinct, attacker-defined targets.

2512.00590.tldr: Wikontic, a multi-stage pipeline that constructs KGs from open-domain text by extracting candidate triplets with qualifiers, enforcing Wikidata-based type and relation constraints, and normalizing entities to reduce duplication, enhances the quality of the generated KG and offers a scalable solution for leveraging structured knowledge in LLMs.

2512.01502.tldr: QVerifier builds a complete model of the policy-environment interaction, incorporates quantum uncertainty directly into the transition probabilities, and then checks safety properties using the Storm model checker, a formal verification method that applies probabilistic model checking to analyze trained QRL policies with and without modeled quantum noise.

2512.02901.tldr: Fairy2i is presented, a universal framework that transforms pre-trained real-valued layers into an equivalent widely-linear complex form, enabling extremely low-bit quantization while reusing existing checkpoints and bridges the gap between the representational efficiency of complex-valued arithmetic and the practical utility of pre-trained models.

2512.04745.tldr: GateMod is introduced, an interpretable theoretically grounded computational model linking the emergence of gating to the underlying decision-making task, and to a neural circuit architecture, offering a unifying framework for neural policy gating, linking task objectives, dynamical computation, and circuit-level mechanisms.

2512.05844.tldr: NEAT, a Neighborhood-guided, Efficient, Autoregressive, Set Transformer that treats molecular graphs as sets of atoms and learns an order-agnostic distribution over admissible tokens at the graph boundary, achieves state-of-the-art performance in autoregressive 3D molecular generation whilst ensuring atom-level permutation invariance by design.

2512.16453.tldr: TimeSeries2Report (TS2R), a semantic translation framework that converts raw lithium-ion battery operational time-series into structured, semantically enriched reports, enabling LLMs to reason, predict, and make decisions in BESS management scenarios, is presented.

2512.18352.tldr: This approach offers the first solution for few-shot EARD, necessitating only the training of a lightweight agent and allowing the LLM to remain training-free, and boosts performance across LLMs and surpasses existing EARD methods in accuracy and earliness.

2512.20014.tldr: This work proposes Visual Attentive Prompting (VAP), a simple-yet-effective training-free perceptual adapter that equips frozen VLAs with top-down selective attention and consistently outperforms generic policies and token-learning baselines in both success rate and correct-object manipulation.

2512.22716.tldr: This framework connects practical memory-based methods with principled reinforcement learning, providing a rigorous mathematical basis for building reflective, memory-embedded agents capable of continual general-purpose learning.

2512.23471.tldr: This paper operationalizes hierarchical density modeling on large language model embeddings in a way not previously explored, framing hierarchical structure as an emergent property of density in embedding spaces, and provides an interpretable, multi-scale representation of semantic structure suitable for large, evolving text collections.

2601.02553.tldr: SimpleMem is introduced, an efficient memory framework based on semantic lossless compression that consistently outperforms baseline approaches in accuracy, retrieval efficiency, and inference cost, demonstrating a superior balance between performance and efficiency.

2601.07568.tldr: The proposed d3LLM (Pseudo-Distilled Diffusion Large Language Model) introduces pseudo-trajectory distillation to teach the model which tokens can be decoded confidently at early steps, thereby improving parallelism and introduces AUP (Accuracy Under Parallelism), a new metric that jointly measures accuracy and parallelism.

2601.11479.tldr: This framework combines a provable approximation algorithm for population coverage optimization with LLM-driven iterative refinement that incorporates human-AI alignment to ensure solutions reflect expert qualitative guidance while preserving coverage guarantees.

2601.14652.tldr: MASOrchestra is proposed, a training-time framework that formulates MAS orchestration as a function-calling reinforcement learning problem with holistic orchestration, generating an entire MAS at once, achieving consistent improvements on public benchmarks including mathematical reasoning, multi-hop QA, and search-based QA, while achieving more than 10x efficiency over strong baselines.

2601.17868.tldr: VidLaDA, a Video LLM based on Diffusion Language Models (DLMs) that leverages bidirectional attention to unlock comprehensive spatiotemporal modeling and decode tokens in parallel is proposed and MARS-Cache, an acceleration strategy that prunes redundancy by combining asynchronous visual cache refreshing with frame-wise chunk attention is introduced.

2601.17915.tldr: EoG (Explanations over Graphs), a disaggregated framework in which an LLM performs bounded local evidence mining and labeling while a deterministic controller manages traversal, state, and belief propagation to compute a minimal explanatory frontier, is proposed.

2601.18537.tldr: A semantic-key-point-conditioned trajectory modeling framework, in which future trajectories are predicted by conditioning on a high-level Next Key Point (NKP) that captures navigational intent, which consistently outperforms state-of-the-art approaches, particularly for long travel durations, directional accuracy, and fine-grained trajectory prediction.

2601.18641.tldr: The study calls for inclusive technological design, anti-bias training to minimize the impact of discriminatory algorithmic decisions, and enforceable policy reform that explicitly recognize speech diversity as a matter of equity, not merely accessibility.

2601.19967.tldr: This work proposes Perturbation-Induced Linearization (PIL), a computationally efficient yet effective method that generates perturbations using only linear surrogate models and reveals a key mechanism underlying unlearnable examples: inducing linearization to deep models, which explains why PIL can achieve competitive results in a very short time.

2601.20487.tldr: It is found that cooperative norms are flexible enough to extend to artificial agents, blurring the boundary between humans and AI in collective decision-making and suggesting that cooperative norms are flexible enough to extend to artificial agents.

2601.20539.tldr: A novel multi-agent reasoning framework, referred to as Planning through World Model for Automated Heuristic Design via Self-Evolving LLMs (PathWise), which formulates heuristic generation as a sequential decision process over an entailment graph serving as a compact, stateful memory of the search trajectory.

2601.20847.tldr: These findings indicate that combining affordable camera and IMU sensors with multimodal attention mechanisms provides a scalable, robust foundation for road surface understanding, particularly relevant for regions where environmental variability and cost constraints limit the adoption of high-end sensing suites.

2601.21233.tldr: This work identifies system prompt extraction as an emergent vulnerability intrinsic to code agents and presents a self-evolving framework that autonomously discovers effective extraction strategies through interaction alone, exposing recurring design- and architecture-level vulnerabilities.

2601.21414.tldr: DAMI is proposed, a framework that estimates a query-specific Reasoning Intensity $\lambda(q)$ to configure cognitive depth and achieves higher accuracy than the Thinking model while remaining efficient, effectively combining the efficiency of System 1 with the reasoning depth of System 2.

2601.21418.tldr: Difficulty-aware Policy Optimization (DiPO), a reinforcement learning-based LRM training framework that encourages LRM to spontaneously model task complexity, and integrates them into reinforcement learning framework to adjust the generation preferences introduced by post-training.

2601.21433.tldr: Audited 16 models across 14 ethical scenarios and found that open-source models endorse prohibited actions 77% of the time under simple negation and 100% under compound negation -- a 317% increase over affirmative framing.

2601.21439.tldr: It is established that instruction-tuned models can decouple logical rule-adherence from persuasive narratives, offering a source of decision stability that complements, and even potentially de-biases, human judgment in institutional contexts.

2601.21444.tldr: Spava is proposed, a sequence-parallel framework with optimized attention that accelerates long-video inference across multiple GPUs and reduces computation and increases parallelism, enabling efficient processing of more visual embeddings without compression and thereby improving task performance.

2601.21453.tldr: This paper proposes LION, a modality-aware geometric manifold grounded in Clifford algebra and decoupled graph neural paradigm based on the Clifford algebra and decoupled graph neural paradigm to implement alignment-then-fusion in multimodal-attributed graphs, and proposes adaptive holographic aggregation to improve modality fusion.

2601.21464.tldr: CoNL is introduced, a framework that unifies generation, evaluation, and meta-evaluation through multi-agent self-play, without external judges or ground truth, and achieves consistent improvements over self-rewarding baselines while maintaining stable training.

2601.21465.tldr: Topeax is demonstrated to be better at both cluster recovery and cluster description than Top2Vec and BERTopic, while also exhibiting less erratic behaviour in response to changing sample size and hyperparameters.

2601.21469.tldr: Results indicate that collaborative protocols can mitigate limitations of small-parameter models and provide a scalable, efficient approach to high-quality automated software engineering.

2601.21473.tldr: ScaleSim is presented, a memory-efficient LLM serving system for large-scale multi-agent simulations that enables proactive prefetching and priority-based eviction, supports diverse agent-specific memory through a modular interface, and achieves up to 1.74x speedup over SGLang on simulation benchmarks.

2601.21477.tldr: It is proved horizon-dependent locality: for finite-horizon problems, an agent's optimal policy at time t depends strictly on its (T-t)-hop neighborhood, rendering the infinite-dimensional control problem tractable and underpins a novel Dynamic Programming Principle on the lifted space of neighborhood distributions.

2601.21498.tldr: SimGraph is introduced, a unified framework that integrates scene graph-based image generation and editing, enabling precise control over object interactions, layouts, and spatial coherence, and outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods.

2601.21505.tldr: The first human evaluation of activation steering concerning the emotional tone of LLM outputs is presented, collecting over 7,000 crowd-sourced ratings from 190 participants via Prolific and support activation-based control as a scalable method for steering LLM behavior across affective dimensions.

2601.21511.tldr: The results demonstrate that signals derived from code can effectively bias LLM-driven algorithm evolution, bridging the gap between code structure and human-understandable performance feedback in automated algorithm design.

2601.21531.tldr: This work proposes the Compression-AliGnEd attack (CAGE), which aligns perturbation optimization with compression inference without assuming access to the deployed compression mechanism or its token budget, and shows that CAGE consistently achieves lower robust accuracy than the baseline.

2601.21533.tldr: This work introduces ARGORA, a framework that organizes multi-expert discussions into explicit argumentation graphs showing which arguments support or attack each other, and casts these graphs as causal models, which can systematically remove individual arguments and recompute outcomes.

2601.21545.tldr: This work presents ShardMemo, a budgeted tiered memory service with Tier A per-agent working state, Tier B sharded evidence with shard-local approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) indexes, and Tier C, a versioned skill library, which enforces scope-before-routing: structured eligibility constraints mask ineligible shards before routing or ANN search.

2601.21547.tldr: Expert Modulation is proposed, a new paradigm for multi-modal time series prediction that conditions both routing and expert computation on textual signals, enabling direct and efficient cross-modal control over expert behavior.

2601.21548.tldr: This work bridges neuroscience-inspired hardware with real-world robotic control, showing that brain-inspired approaches can tackle fast-paced interaction tasks while supporting always-on learning in intelligent machines.

2601.21561.tldr: This work proposes Selective Adaptive Learning (SAL), a training method that combines selective parameter activation with adaptive area partitioning that decomposes the parameter space into mutually exclusive, sample-dependent regions and mitigates gradient interference across divergent semantic patterns.

2601.21570.tldr: This work establishes a foundation for self-evolving embodied intelligence, accelerating the paradigm shift from labor-intensive manual tuning to scalable, autonomous engineering in embodied AI field.

2601.21572.tldr: Inspired by trust-region methods in reinforcement learning that constrain policy updates in distribution space, SATR is proposed, a distributional update rule that constrains relative change by bounding KL divergence normalized by an estimated signal energy.

2601.21576.tldr: This paper proposes ALiCoT (Aligned Implicit CoT), a novel framework that overcomes the signal decay by aligning latent token distributions with intermediate reasoning states and achieves a 54.4x speedup while maintaining performance comparable to explicit CoT.

2601.21582.tldr: A modular framework of depth-recurrent attention mixtures (Dreamer), combining sequence attention, depth attention, and sparse expert attention is introduced, which alleviates the hidden-size bottleneck through attention along depth, decouples scaling dimensions, and allows depth-recurrent models to scale efficiently and effectively.

2601.21590.tldr: A theoretically grounded alternative that eliminates the need for iterative MCMC is proposed, and a novel formulation showing that the global power distribution can be approximated by a token-level scaled low-temperature one, where the scaling factor captures future trajectory quality.
