2604.04319.tldr: An incentive-compatible experimental methodology based on diagram generation tasks, in which errors in generative AI output and test effects on user reliance are induced, finds that people are not averse to jaggedness in this experimental setting, and encourages future work that varies task difficulty at the same time as other features of AI errors.

2604.04324.tldr: This work curates a benchmark of 500 papers from the IEEE Conference on Decision and Control and proposes RESCORE, a three component LLM agentic framework, Analyzer, Coder, and Verifier that achieves an estimated 10X speedup over manual human replication, drastically cutting the time and effort required to verify published control methodologies.

2604.04331.tldr: The key innovation of this work lies in leveraging generation to assist in reconstructing occluded regions, and introduces a learnable authenticity scalar for each Gaussian primitive, which dynamically modulates opacity during splatting for authenticity-aware rendering and supervision.

2604.04339.tldr: This work introduces a thermodynamics-inspired explainable geospatial AI framework that integrates statistical mechanics with graph neural networks and demonstrates that thermodynamic constraints can improve the interpretability of GeoAI while preserving strong predictive performance in complex spatial systems.

2604.04341.tldr: This paper tries to get a language-model-based agent to react to threats of burning money in the same way it would react to"normal"threats, and proposes four different methods, using techniques of prompting, fine-tuning, and scaffolding.

2604.04347.tldr: RoboPhD introduces validation-free evolution: instead of splitting the budget between training and validation, it uses Elo competition on training data to simultaneously evaluate agents and drive evolution, and is released as a versatile toolkit under the MIT license with a simple optimize_anything() API for evolving diverse complex agents.

2604.04353.tldr: Results show that ReFinE effectively synthesizes and contextualizes design implications, reducing cognitive load and improving designers'ability to integrate research evidence into UI mockups.

2604.04356.tldr: This work proposes a novel method, Router-weighted Expert Activation Merging (REAM), which instead of removing experts, groups them and merges their weights, better preserving original performance and reveals a trade-off between MC and GEN performance that depends on the mix of calibration data.

2604.04359.tldr: This work proposes GroundedKG-RAG, a RAG system in which the knowledge graph is explicitly extracted from and grounded in the source document, and finds that it performs on par with a state-of-the art proprietary long-context model at smaller cost and outperforms a competitive baseline.

2604.04363.tldr: A theoretical analysis and empirical evaluations of a novel set of techniques for computational cost reduction of test time operations of network classifiers based on extreme learning machine (ELM) show that the classification at test time can be performed using solely integer operations without compromising the classification accuracy.

2604.04364.tldr: This work introduces CONTXT (Contextual augmentatiOn for Neural feaTure X Transforms), a simple and intuitive method for contextual adaptation that provides a compact way to steer information flow and neural processing without retraining.

2604.04373.tldr: It is shown that effective context construction critically depends on experience, and a detailed analysis of experience-augmented agents is presented, studying how to derive context from experience, how performance scales with accumulated experience, what characterizes good context, and which data structures best support context construction.

2604.04374.tldr: This work proposes considerate human-robot coexistence, arguing that humans act not only as design contributors but also as interpreters and mediators who actively shape how robots are understood and integrated across deployment stages.

2604.04383.tldr: This work introduces an LLM-powered multi-agent simulation (LLM-MAS) framework for optimizing service operations and develops an on-trajectory learning algorithm that, on a single simulation run, simultaneously constructs zeroth-order gradient estimates and updates design parameters to optimize steady-state performance.

2604.04386.tldr: A new math benchmark generation pipeline is proposed that uses AI-generated hypotheses to identify the specific math concepts and skills that LLMs struggle with, and then generates new benchmark problems targeting these weaknesses.

2604.04399.tldr: GUIDE (GUI Understanding and Interpretable Diagnostic Evaluation), a framework that decomposes trajectory assessment into three sequential stages mirroring the compositional structure of GUI tasks, substantially outperforms existing evaluators and mitigates the context overload that degrades existing evaluators as task complexity grows.

2604.04410.tldr: The proposed alignment method is statistically consistent and yields significantly tighter convergence guarantees than DDRO, and is based on the relative density ratio between the preferred data distribution and a mixture of the preferred and non-preferred data distributions.

2604.04411.tldr: This study reveals that there is a clear gap between internal representations and generated responses, and information required to solve the VDU task is often encoded more linearly from intermediate layers than from the final layer.

2604.04420.tldr: This work proposes a simple yet effective SinglePrompt that eliminates the need for prompt selection and focuses on classifier optimization, and achieves state-of-the-art performance across various online continual learning benchmarks.

2604.04426.tldr: ShieldNet is proposed, a network-level guardrail framework that detects supply-chain poisoning by observing real network interactions rather than surface-level tool traces, and substantially outperforming existing MCP scanners and LLM-based guardrails.

2604.04448.tldr: STEP, a dataset that models CBT counseling by explicitly reflecting automatic thoughts alongside dynamic, action-level counseling sequences, is introduced and STEPPER, a counseling agent that proactively elicits automatic thoughts and executes cognitively grounded interventions is trained.

2604.04450.tldr: This work proposes an end-to-end method to obtain modular and explainable control over LLM outputs through ontological definitions of aspects related to the conversation, and demonstrates the effectiveness of ontology-driven control in conversational systems.

2604.04456.tldr: A novel metric aimed at assessing the consistency of model explanations, ensuring that models consistently reflect the intended objectives and consistency under label-preserving perturbations is proposed, and provides a deeper understanding of model behavior by enabling more robust verification of rationale stability.

2604.04461.tldr: DP-OPD improves perplexity over DP fine-tuning and off-policy DP distillation, and outperforms synthesis-based DP distillation, and outperforms synthesis-based DP distillation while substantially simplifying the training pipeline.

2604.04465.tldr: This paper identifies a structural limitation in current multimodal AI architectures that is topological rather than parametric, and proposes UOO implementation via Neural ODEs with topological regularization, the ANALOGY-MM benchmark with error-type-ratio metric, and the META-TOP three-tier benchmark testing cross-civilizational topological isomorphism across seven archetypes.

2604.04468.tldr: RetailSim is presented, an end-to-end retail simulation framework that models this pipeline in a unified environment, explicitly designed for simulation fidelity through diverse product spaces, persona-driven agents, and multi-turn interactions.

2604.04470.tldr: The results suggest that test-time generative posterior refinement is a practical route to reduce MC misses and improve robustness without additional real dense labeling.

2604.04474.tldr: MAVEN is introduced, a mesh-aware volumetric encoding network for simulating 3D flexible deformation, which explicitly models geometric mesh elements of higher dimension to achieve a more accurate and natural physical simulation.

2604.04475.tldr: This work proposes \textsc{FeDPM}, a federated framework for time-series foundation models based on discrete prototypical memories that align cross-domain memories to promote a unified discrete latent space and introduces a domain-specific memory update mechanism to balance shared and personalized prototypical knowledge.

2604.04482.tldr: A scalable, interpretable pipeline for predicting population-level watching, pausing, skipping, and rewinding behavior as proxies for cognitive load from video content alone is proposed and demonstrates the feasibility of cost-efficient, interpretable pre-screening of educational video design.

2604.04485.tldr: A 1D Inception-v1 model trained with ArcFace on an internal clinical corpus of 164,440 12-lead ECGs from 53,079 patients and tested it on larger cohorts derived from MIMIC-IV-ECG and HEEDB, showing monotonic degradation as gallery size increased and recovery as more examinations per patient became available.

2604.04493.tldr: SLaB is proposed, a novel framework that decomposes each linear layer weight into three complementary components: a sparse matrix, a low-rank matrix, and a binary matrix that eliminates the need for retraining and leverages activation-aware pruning scores to guide the decomposition process.

2604.04497.tldr: This paper introduces Multi-Objective Control (MOC), which trains a single LLM to directly generate responses in the preference-defined regions of the Pareto front, and introduces multi-objective optimization (MOO) principles into RLHF to train an LLM as a preference-conditioned policy network.

2604.04514.tldr: This work presents SuperLocalMemory V3.3, a local-first agent memory system implementing the full cognitive memory taxonomy with mathematical lifecycle dynamics, and introduces five contributions, including a new metric on the Gaussian statistical manifold achieving 100% precision at preferring high-fidelity embeddings over quantized ones.

2604.04518.tldr: This reproducibility study evaluates recently proposed correction methods based on explainable artificial intelligence techniques alongside popular non-XAI baselines using both synthetic and real-world datasets, and shows that XAI-based methods generally outperform non-XAI approaches.

2604.04527.tldr: Encapsulated Substitution and Agentic Refinement on a Live Scaffold for Safe C-to-Rust Translation, a two-phase pipeline for translating real-world C projects to safe Rust, shows substantial unsafe-construct reduction across all 15 programs while maintaining full test-vector correctness.

2604.04528.tldr: Drifting MPC is proposed, an offline trajectory optimization framework that combines drifting generative models with receding-horizon planning under unknown dynamics and can generate near-optimal trajectories while retaining the one-step inference efficiency of drifting models and substantially reducing generation time relative to diffusion-based baselines.

2604.04532.tldr: Results indicate that language should be treated as an explicit evaluation variable in agentic benchmarks, and show that changing the judge's language can invert backbone rankings.

2604.04561.tldr: A systematic taxonomy based on approximately 10,000 trials across seven models, 37 prompt conditions, and 12 hypothesized attack dimensions shows a pattern consistent with improving safety training, though model capability differences are a confounder.

2604.04589.tldr: This work proposes two complementary strategies for port-selection in fluid antenna multiple access (FAMA) systems with multi-port fluid antenna (FA) receivers: GFwd+S, a greedy forward-selection method with swap refinement that consistently outperforms state-of-the-art reference schemes in terms of SE, and a Transformer-based neural network trained via imitation learning followed by a Reinforce policy-gradient stage.

2604.04593.tldr: This work proposes Contrastive Hypothesis Retrieval (CHR), a framework inspired by the process of clinical differential diagnosis that bridges clinical reasoning with retrieval mechanism design and offers a practical path to reducing hard-negative contamination in medical RAG systems.

2604.04603.tldr: The goal is to design a framework that is lightweight, easy to construct, and capable of providing accurate estimates with satisfying online efficiency, which includes updating algorithm designed to efficiently support large-scale dynamic scenarios of data updates.

2604.04604.tldr: This paper provides the first systematic regulatory mapping for AI agent providers integrating draft harmonised standards under Standardisation Request M/613 to CEN/CENELEC JTC 21 as of January 2026, and proposes a twelve-step compliance architecture and a regulatory trigger mapping connecting agent actions to applicable legislation.

2604.04634.tldr: This work introduces a comprehensive dataset and a novel detection framework built on the Qwen2.5-VL Vision Transformer, which operates natively at variable spatial resolutions and temporal durations and preserves the high-frequency artifacts and spatiotemporal inconsistencies typically lost during conventional preprocessing.

2604.04637.tldr: A minimal architecture is presented in which a slow perspective latent $g$ feeds back into perception and is itself updated through perceptual processing, which identifies a minimal mechanism for history-dependent perspectival organization in artificial agents.

2604.04646.tldr: The Flow Divergence Sampler is proposed, a training-free framework that refines intermediate states before each solver step that consistently improves fidelity across various generation tasks including text-to-image synthesis, and inverse problems.

2604.04651.tldr: Policy, a lightweight fine-tuning approach that explicitly trains SLMs to reliably retrieve and generate answers grounded in retrieved evidence, is proposed, achieving LLM-level results across benchmarks.

2604.04655.tldr: Through finite-size scaling of gradient avalanche dynamics across eight model scales, grokking is a dimensional phase transition that crosses from sub-diffusive to super-diffusive at generalization onset, exhibiting self-organized criticality (SOC).

2604.04660.tldr: The term Artificial Retainer is introduced for this category: a non-human system with persistent memory, defined authority, domain-specific autonomy, and forensic accountability in an ongoing relationship with a specific principal -- distinguished from software assistants and autonomous agents, drawing on professional retainer relationships and the bounded autonomy of trained working animals.

2604.04664.tldr: ROSClaw is an agent framework for heterogeneous robots that integrates policy learning and task execution within a unified vision-language model (VLM) controller, establishing an autonomous closed-loop framework that minimizes the reliance on robot-specific development workflows.

2604.04670.tldr: The details of the implementation (including the prompt to the LLM, and code), and how the RAG pipeline was designed and tuned to meet course needs are provided, and student feedback revealed that the AI-TA was beneficial, while students had mixed feelings about preferring it over human tutoring.

2604.04690.tldr: Pickalo, a modular 6D pose-based bin-picking pipeline built entirely on low-cost hardware, and ablation studies demonstrate the benefits of enhanced depth estimation and of the pose buffer for long-term stability and throughput in realistic industrial conditions.

2604.04692.tldr: Experimental results on three datasets show that incorporating the Analyzer's assessment of visual evidence necessity into the Verifier's prediction yields substantial improvements in verification performance, and this work proposes AMuFC, a multimodal fact-checking framework that employs two collaborative agents with distinct roles for the adaptive use of visual evidence.

2604.04701.tldr: Mixed-to-Uniform Quantization detects outlier channels in input activations and introduces a small auxiliary matrix that redistributes outlier magnitudes across channels, thereby alleviating the outlier problem and suggesting that MUXQ provides a promising direction for efficient and accurate LLM inference on edge devices.

2604.04708.tldr: BiST, a rigorously curated Bangla-English corpus for sentence-level grammatical classification, annotated across two fundamental dimensions: syntactic structure and tense, establishes a unified resource for bilingual grammatical modeling and facilitates linguistically grounded multilingual research.

2604.04717.tldr: Machine learning models have achieved high accuracies in spectroscopic classification, without a clear proof that those models used chemical features, but it is unclear how those models used chemical features.

2604.04720.tldr: This work defines a suite of measurable reasoning features spanning multilingual alignment, reasoning step, and reasoning flow aspects of reasoning traces, and uses logistic regression to quantify how each feature associates with final answer accuracy.

2604.04723.tldr: The findings suggest that evaluations on clean standard English may overestimate real-world model performance, and that evaluating ESL variation and typographical errors in isolation does not fully capture model behavior in realistic settings.

2604.04727.tldr: The key limitations of classical complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor (CMOS) technology are surveyed and how cross-layer neuromorphic approaches may overcome them are outlined.

2604.04732.tldr: A preliminary computational audit of cultural inclusivity in a creative writing task finds that the model exhibits stereotyped metaphor usage for certain settings, as well as Western defaultism, suggesting that merely prompting an LLM with a cultural identity does not guarantee culturally grounded reasoning.

2604.04733.tldr: This work proposes a Reinforcement Learning (RL)-based framework to automatically discover the failure modes or blind spots of any candidate VLM on a given data distribution without human intervention, and identifies 36 novel failure modes in which VLMs struggle.

2604.04736.tldr: This work introduces sampling parallelism, a simple yet powerful parallelization strategy that targets the primary bottleneck of sampling-based Bayesian learning: the samples themselves, and demonstrates that sampling parallelism is complementary to existing strategies by implementing a hybrid approach that combines sample and data parallelism.

2604.04741.tldr: The thematic analysis highlights both the promises and limitations of AI-driven cost reduction in higher education, offering insights for policymakers, university administrators, and educators on the economic implications of AI adoption, while also pointing to gaps that warrant further empirical research.

2604.04743.tldr: A geometric dynamical systems framework in which hallucinations arise from task-dependent basin structure in latent space is presented, which formalizes this behavior with task-complexity and multi-basin theorems, characterize basin emergence in L-layer transformers, and shows that geometry-aware steering can reduce hallucination probability without retraining.

2604.04749.tldr: It is argued that telemetry-first AI governance represents a categorical architectural shift in how enterprise trust is produced and demonstrated and is evaluated across ISO 42001, the EU AI Act, SOC 2, GDPR, and HIPAA.

2604.04757.tldr: The results show that transcript auditing alone cannot rule out covert coordination between AI agents, and identify a new cryptographic theory that may be of independent interest.

2604.04759.tldr: The first real-world safety evaluation of OpenClaw is presented and the CIK taxonomy is introduced, which unifies an agent's persistent state into three dimensions, i.e., Capability, Identity, and Knowledge, for safety analysis, showing that the vulnerabilities are inherent to the agent architecture.

2604.04767.tldr: Cog-DRIFT is introduced, a framework that constructs reformulated variants and organizes them into an adaptive curriculum based on difficulty, enabling the model to learn from problems that previously yielded zero signal under standard RL post-training.

2604.04786.tldr: This work reformulate magic square construction as a quantum search problem in which a reversible, constraint-sensitive oracle marks valid configurations for amplitude amplification via Grover's algorithm, and benchmarks the quantum approach against classical brute-force enumeration and backtracking.

2604.04808.tldr: The Decision-Relevant Selection algorithm, which selects a subset of concepts from a candidate set, along with performance bounds relating the selected concepts to the performance of the resulting policy, improves the effectiveness of test-time concept interventions across reinforcement learning benchmarks and real-world healthcare environments.

2604.04820.tldr: This work presents ANX, an open, extensible, verifiable agent-native protocol and top-level framework integrating CLI, Skill, MCP, resolving pain points via protocol innovation, architectural optimization and tool supplementation and ensures native security.

2604.04843.tldr: A coarse-to-fine instruction-conditioned interaction generation framework that leverages trajectories from the preceding refinement to update scene context and condition subsequent refinement at each denoising step of consistency model, yielding consistent interactions.

2604.04852.tldr: This study proposes a structured prompt engineering framework designed to strengthen CoT reasoning integrity while improving security threat and attack detection reliability in local LLM deployments, and introduces explicit reasoning controls to mitigate hallucination and prevent reasoning drift.

2604.04853.tldr: Results show that preserving episodic ground truth while layering adaptive retrieval yields robust, efficient long-term memory for personalized LLM agents, and MemMachine is the most cost-efficient setup.

2604.04875.tldr: This work forms video mashup creation as a Multimodal Coherency Coherency Satisfaction Problem (MMCSP) and proposes the DIRECT framework, a hierarchical multi-agent framework that significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in both objective metrics and human subjective evaluation.

2604.04876.tldr: It is proved that for any fixed sound computably enumerable verifier, there exists a threshold beyond which true policy-compliant instances cannot be certified once their complexity exceeds that threshold, and no finite formal verifier can certify all policy-compliant instances of arbitrarily high complexity.

2604.04878.tldr: This work introduces a novel approach with three complementary measurements: learning, potential, and retention, to disentangle performance changes caused by model adaptations versus dynamic environments, to disentangle performance changes caused by model adaptations versus dynamic environments.

2604.04891.tldr: This paper introduces a family of Spectral Wasserstein distances indexed by a norm gamma on positive semidefinite matrices, and proves the equivalence between the static and dynamic Benamou-Brenier formulations, and shows that the induced Gaussian covariance cost is also a metric.

2604.04894.tldr: This work conceptually decomposes policy entropy into informative entropy, which preserves diverse solution paths, and spurious entropy, which erodes reasoning patterns, and proposes AsymGRPO, an exploratory framework that explicitly decouples the modulation of positive and negative rollouts.

2604.04895.tldr: This work proposes a paradigm shift towards Agentic-FL, a framework where Language Model-based Agents (LMagents) assume autonomous orchestration roles, and demonstrates how server-side agents can mitigate selection bias through contextual reasoning, while client-side agents act as local guardians, dynamically managing privacy budgets and adapting model complexity to hardware constraints.

2604.04898.tldr: The QED-Nano model, a 4B model post-trained for Olympiad-level proofs, surpasses the proof-generation performance of much larger open models, including Nomos-1 and GPT-OSS-120B, and approaches the performance of proprietary models like Gemini 3 Pro, at a fraction of the inference cost.

2604.04901.tldr: Extensive experiments show that FileGramBench remains challenging for state-of-the-art memory systems and that FileGramEngine and FileGramOS are effective, and by open-sourcing the framework, it hopes to support future research on personalized memory-centric file-system agents.

2604.04906.tldr: The main result identifies a threshold in the speed of updating: when the aggregator updates too quickly, there is no positive-measure set of training weights that robustly improves learning across a broad class of environments, whereas such weights exist when updating is sufficiently slow.

2604.04914.tldr: This paper presents a generic formulation for symbolic properties, with monotonicity and robustness as concrete examples, and shows how they can be analyzed using existing DNN verification engines, and encodes symbolic properties as comparisons between related executions of the same policy and decomposes them into practically tractable sub-properties.

2604.04924.tldr: This work shows that these pre-trained diffusion models inherently possess restoration behavior, which can be unlocked by directly learning prompt embeddings at the output of the text encoder, Interestingly, this behavior is largely inaccessible through text prompts and text-token embedding optimization.

2604.04930.tldr: This work proposes CoDE-Stop (Confidence Dynamics Early Stop), an early stopping method that leverages the dynamics of intermediate answer confidence to decide when to terminate reasoning, requiring no additional training and easily integrating into existing models.

2410.19940.tldr: Cobblestone, a divide-and-conquer approach for proof synthesis, is introduced and research shows that tools can make use of partial progress and external input to more effectively automate formal verification.

2410.20791.tldr: Critical issues in FM(s) selection, data and model alignment, prompt engineering, agent orchestration, system testing, and deployment are identified, alongside cross-cutting concerns such as memory management, observability, and feedback integration.

2411.08249.tldr: This paper advocates that the dynamic and event-driven nature of time-series data makes RAG a crucial component of TSFMs and introduces a principled RAG framework for time-series forecasting, called Retrieval Augmented Forecasting (RAF).

2501.14194.tldr: Enter, an interpretable Video Question Answering (VideoQA) system based on event graphs that outperform existing top-down approaches while obtaining competitive performance against bottom-up approaches and offers superior interpretability and explainability in the reasoning process.

2502.10573.tldr: An entropy-based model selection framework that quantifies dataset complexity to recommend suitable algorithms, and the DAW-Transformer (Dynamic Attribute-Wise Transformer), which integrates multi-head attention with a dynamic windowing mechanism to capture long-range dependencies across all attributes are presented.

2504.19959.tldr: UVM2, an automated verification framework that leverages Large Language Models (LLMs) to generate UVM testbenches and iteratively refine them using coverage feedback, significantly reducing manual effort while maintaining rigorous verification standards is presented.

2505.00472.tldr: Experimental results demonstrate that the framework autonomously enables efficient intent processing and real-time monitoring, while balancing reasoning quality and computational efficiency, particularly under resource-constrained edge conditions.

2506.22653.tldr: This work highlights the architecture of URSA, a scientific agent ecosystem for accelerating research tasks that consists of a set of modular agents and tools that can be combined to address scientific problems of varied complexity and impact.

2507.05201.tldr: This work introduces MedGemma, a collection of medical vision-language foundation models based on Gemma 3 4B and 27B that demonstrates advanced medical understanding and reasoning on images and text, significantly exceeding the performance of similar-sized generative models and approaching the performance of task-specific models, while maintaining the general capabilities of the Gemma 3 base models.

2507.22418.tldr: This paper leverages conditional flow matching, a simulation-free flow-based generative model that learns an exact density, to produce highly accurate segmentation results and generates uncertainty maps that provide deeper insights into the reliability of the segmentation outcomes.

2603.07339.tldr: Agora is an early-stage AI-powered platform that uses LLMs to organize authentic human voices on policy issues, helping users build consensus-finding skills by proposing and revising policy recommendations, hearing supporting and opposing perspectives, and receiving feedback on how policy changes affect predicted support.

2603.20231.tldr: HR Simulator, a game where users roleplay as an HR officer and write emails to tackle challenging workplace scenarios, is evaluated with GPT-4o as a judge based on scenario-specific rubrics and suggests large language models could substantially reshape communication in the workplace if they are widely adopted in professional correspondence.

2603.22346.tldr: It is shown that model independence largely neutralizes first-mover bias, and DASH provides two diagnostic tools -- the Feature Stability Index and Importance-Stability Plot -- that detect first-mover bias without ground truth.

2603.28251.tldr: DiffAttn is proposed, a diffusion-based framework that formulates this task as a conditional diffusion-denoising process, enabling more accurate modeling of drivers' attention and has the potential to improve in-cabin human-machine interaction, risk perception, and drivers' Tate measurement in intelligent vehicles.

2604.01346.tldr: This paper surveys the world model landscape; introduces formal definitions of trajectory persistence and representational risk; presents a five-profile attacker taxonomy; and proposes interdisciplinary mitigations spanning adversarial hardening, alignment engineering, NIST AI RMF and EU AI Act governance, and human-factors design, arguing that world models require the same rigour as flight-control software or medical devices.

2604.01619.tldr: This work demonstrates that sparse autoencoders trained on foundation-model features yield monosemantic, spatially grounded neurons that consistently activate on meaningful morphological parts, and introduces a trait annotation pipeline that localizes salient regions and uses vision-language prompting to generate interpretable trait descriptions.

2604.04387.tldr: Gradual Cognitive Externalization (GCE), a framework arguing that ambient AI systems, through sustained causal coupling with users, transition from modeling cognitive functions to constituting part of users' cognitive architectures, is proposed.

2604.04721.tldr: Although AI assistance improves performance in the short-term, people perform significantly worse without AI and are more likely to give up, suggesting the need for AI model development to prioritize scaffolding long-term competence alongside immediate task completion.

2604.04987.tldr: This work formalizes the speculative sampling algorithm through the lens of constrained optimization and proposes Cactus (constrained acceptance speculative sampling), a method that guarantees controlled divergence from the verifier distribution and increasing acceptance rates.

2604.04990.tldr: This work identifies five mechanisms by which agents make implicit architectural choices and proposes six prompt-architecture coupling patterns that map natural-language prompt features to the infrastructure they require and identifies the phenomenon vibe architecting, architecture shaped by prompts rather than deliberate design.

2604.04992.tldr: Emotional context is established as a measurable attack surface with implications for real-world AI deployment in high-stress domains and FreakOut-LLM, a framework investigating whether emotional context compromises safety alignment in adversarial settings is introduced.

2604.04997.tldr: It is found that generative Vision-Language Models (VLMs) like Qwen2.5-VL, enhanced with Chain-of-Thought prompting, achieve superior zero-shot accuracy compared to state-of-the-art multimodal embedding models like QQMM.

2604.04999.tldr: PRIME is proposed, a missing-aware multimodal self-supervised pretraining framework that learns robust and transferable representations from partially observed cohorts that remain predictive under arbitrary modality subsets under structured missingness augmentation.

2604.05000.tldr: The results indicate that bounded, traceable lifecycle automation is practical when autonomy is embedded within explicit control, recovery, and audit mechanisms.

2604.05007.tldr: The proposed Binaural Difference Attention with Action Transition Prediction framework jointly optimizes perception and policy and achieves state-of-the-art Success Rates across most settings, underscore BDATP's superior generalization capability and its robustness across diverse navigation architectures.

2604.05011.tldr: The Yemeni Music Classification Model (YMCM), a convolutional neural network (CNN)-based system designed to classify music genres from time-frequency features, is proposed, and experimental findings reveal that YMCM is the most effective, achieving the highest accuracy of 98.8% with Mel-spectrogram features.

2604.05012.tldr: This work conducts an empirical study of three state-of-the-art KV cache management frameworks: vLLM, InfiniGen, and H2O, revealing the most suitable selection and configuration of KV cache strategies under memory and performance constraints.

2604.05013.tldr: This work proposes a novel scaling paradigm that shifts the focus from task-level optimization to atomic skill mastery, and observes that improvements in these atomic skills generalize well to other unseen composite coding tasks, such as bug-fixing, code refactoring, machine learning engineering, and code security.

2604.05014.tldr: To the best knowledge, StarVLA is one of the most comprehensive open-source VLA frameworks available, and is expected to lower the barrier for reproducing existing methods and prototyping new ones.

2604.05018.tldr: PaperOrchestra is introduced, a multi-agent framework for automated AI research paper writing that flexibly transforms unconstrained pre-writing materials into submission-ready LaTeX manuscripts, including comprehensive literature synthesis and generated visuals, such as plots and conceptual diagrams.

2604.05030.tldr: The competitiveness of an architecture whose native operations are complex-valued superposition and conjugate retrieval is consistent with recent empirical evidence that semantic interpretation in both humans and large language models exhibits non-classical contextuality, and what this implies for the choice of computational formalism in language modeling is discussed.

2604.05039.tldr: The proposed ID-Sim metric, a feed-forward metric designed to faithfully reflect human selective sensitivity, is evaluated on a new unified evaluation benchmark for assessing consistency with human annotations across identity-focused recognition, retrieval, and generative tasks.

2604.05051.tldr: It is demonstrated that LLM responses in medical QA can be systematically influenced through query phrasing alone, even when grounded in the same evidence, highlighting the importance of phrasing robustness as an evaluation criterion for RAG-based systems in high-stakes settings.

2604.05064.tldr: DynLMC is introduced, a Dynamic Linear Model of Coregionalization that incorporates time-varying, regime-switching correlations and cross-channel lag structures, and produces synthetic multivariate time series with correlation dynamics that closely resemble real data.

2604.05066.tldr: The tool handles arbitrary affine loop nests, covering workloads such as tensor contractions, einsum expressions, stencil computations, and general polyhedral programs, and the sequence of Barvinok counting operations used to derive symbolic reuse-interval and reuse-distance distributions.

2604.05070.tldr: A part-edge refinement module that enforces exclusive Gaussian ownership and a kinematic reasoning head that predicts joint positions and hinge axes of movable parts enable faithful part-aware simulation, bridging the gap between static generation and animatable vehicle models.

2604.05075.tldr: MMORF is presented, a framework for constructing language model-based multi-agent systems (MAS) for multi-objective retrosynthesis planning that achieves strong safety and cost metrics on soft-constraint tasks, frequently Pareto-dominating baseline routes, and outperforming state-of-the-art baselines.

2604.05077.tldr: A stratified Hierarchical Graph Attention Network (HGAT) that captures spatial and thermal dependencies across scan tracks and deposited layers, and a feature-importance-aware anisotropic Gaussian mechanism (FI-LDP) for non-interactive feature privatization is proposed.

2604.05080.tldr: Nidus is presented, a governance runtime that mechanizes the V-model for AI-assisted software delivery that externalizes the engineering methodology into a decidable artifact verified on every mutation before persistence.

2604.05081.tldr: Beyond its improved multimodal performance over MedGemma 1, MedGemma 1.5 improves on text-based clinical knowledge and reasoning, improving by 5% on MedQA accuracy and 22% on EHRQA accuracy.

2604.05083.tldr: The OmniScore family of complementary, deterministic learned metrics developed using small size parameter models approximates LLM-judge behavior while preserving the low latency and consistency of traditional model-based scoring.

2604.05100.tldr: Six empirically grounded desiderata are proposed and all audit artifacts are released so the community can build instructed code-editing benchmarks whose scores reliably reflect real-world editing capability.

2604.05110.tldr: This work demonstrates the feasibility of simultaneous dual-view mammogram synthesis using a difference-guided DDPM, highlighting its potential for dataset augmentation and future cross-view-aware AI applications in breast imaging.

2604.05112.tldr: This work extends DPT to diverse multi-domain environments, applying Flow Matching as a natural training choice that preserves its interpretation as Bayesian posterior sampling and obtains an agent trained across hundreds of diverse tasks that achieves clear gains in generalization to the held-out test set.

2604.05113.tldr: CRAB is proposed, a post-hoc debiasing strategy for GeneRec that alleviates popularity bias by mitigating frequency imbalance among semantic tokens, and significantly improves recommendation performance by effectively alleviating popularity bias.

2604.05114.tldr: This work constructs high-quality reasoning data through rigorous QA curation from initial structured data for improving long-context reasoning in large language models (LLMs) and facilitates self-distillation, demonstrating $\pi^2$'s usefulness.

2604.05116.tldr: The proposed LDTL framework outperforms existing baselines in diagnostic accuracy under a sequential clinical diagnosis setting, while requiring fewer diagnostic tests, and ablation studies highlight the critical role of trajectory-level posterior alignment in achieving these improvements.

2604.05117.tldr: This work introduces VidGround as a simple yet effective solution: using only the actual visually grounded questions without any linguistic biases for post-training, and shows that data curation with a simple post-training algorithm outperforms several more complex post-training techniques, highlighting that data quality is a major bottleneck for improving video understanding in VLMs.

2604.05125.tldr: This work model policy retrieval for PA as a sequential decision-making problem, formulating adaptive retrieval as a Markov Decision Process (MDP), and trains policies using Conservative Q-Learning, Implicit Q-Learning, and Direct Preference Optimization in an offline RL setting.

2604.05134.tldr: This work analyzes how reasoning evolves in a language model -- from supervised fine-tuning (SFT) to reinforcement learning (RL) -- by analyzing how a set of theoretically-inspired datasets impacts language model performance in chess to surpass leading open-source reasoning models in chess with a 7B-parameter model.

2604.05136.tldr: Experimental results demonstrate that KA-FCMs significantly outperform conventional architectures and achieve competitive accuracy relative to MLPs, while preserving graph- based interpretability and enabling the explicit extraction of mathematical laws from the learned edges.

2604.05137.tldr: EffiPair is introduced, an inference-time iterative refinement framework that operates entirely at test time by generating multiple candidate solutions, identifying informative program pairs with large efficiency gaps, summarizing their execution differences into lightweight feedback, and using this signal to produce more efficient solutions.

2604.05150.tldr: This work introduces a system architecture for constrained LLM-based code generation, a four-stage generation-and-validation pipeline that converts probabilistic model output into production-ready code artifacts, and an evaluation framework measuring operational metrics including token amortization, determinism, reliability, security, and cost.

2604.05157.tldr: IntentScore is proposed, a plan-aware reward model that learns to score candidate actions from 398K offline GUI interaction steps spanning three operating systems, demonstrating that reward estimation learned from heterogeneous offline trajectories generalizes to unseen agents and task distributions.

2604.05159.tldr: The proposed CovQValue method outperforms greedy selection on TestGenEval Lite, achieving 51-77% higher branch coverage across three popular LLMs and winning on 77-84% of targets.

2604.05162.tldr: A fully autonomous Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) framework to control mechanically adjustable metallic reflector arrays is presented, and the efficacy of MARL-driven spatial abstractions as a scalable, highly practical pathway toward AI-empowered wireless networks is validated.

2604.05163.tldr: This work identifies, implements, and evaluates 10 proposed measures of interview response quality to determine which are actually predictive of a response's contribution to the study findings, and finds that direct relevance to a key research question is the strongest predictor of response quality.

2604.05166.tldr: It is found that while participants in the structural mental model condition demonstrate a better understanding of the system, this can have a backfiring effect: while these participants judged the system as more usable, they also produced letters with more grammatical errors, highlighting a complex relationship between system understanding, trust, and control in contexts that require user oversight of error-prone AI outputs.

2604.05168.tldr: A domain-adapted, instruction-following, LLM-driven framework that leverages chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning to parse and structure HPC logs with high fidelity, and develops a hybrid fine-tuning methodology that adapts a general-purpose LLM to domain-specific log data, enabling privacy-preserving, locally deployable, fast, and energy-efficient log-mining approach.

2604.05171.tldr: A modality-aware and anatomically grounded 3D vector-quantized VAE (VQ-VAE) for reconstructing multi-modal brain MRIs, called NeuroQuant, which achieves superior reconstruction fidelity compared to existing VAEs, enabling a scalable foundation for downstream generative modeling and cross-modal brain image analysis.

2604.05182.tldr: The Large Sparse Reconstruction Model is introduced to study how scaling transformer context windows impacts feed-forward 3D reconstruction, showing that expanding the context window remarkably narrows this gap and enables high-fidelity 3D object reconstruction and inverse rendering.

2604.05183.tldr: This paper derives the structure of the manifold formed by the recently proposed Group-and-Shuffle orthogonal matrices, and obtains efficient formulas for the geodesics approximation between two points, and proposes a transform that restores spectral properties of the merged adapter for higher-quality fusion.

2604.05190.tldr: This study systematically explored both encoder- and decoder-based generative LLMs for screening clinical narratives to facilitate clinical trial recruitment and explored three strategies to alleviate the "Lost in the Middle" issue when handling long documents.

2604.05224.tldr: This work introduces AttriBench, the first fame- and demographically-balanced quote attribution benchmark dataset, and introduces and investigates suppression, a distinct failure mode in which models omit attribution entirely, even when the model has access to authorship information.

2604.05226.tldr: It is argued that evaluating modern manipulation policies requires reframing evaluation as a language-driven process over structured physical domains, and RoboPlayground, a framework that enables users to author executable manipulation tasks using natural language within a structured physical domain is presented.

2604.05229.tldr: A layered translation method is proposed that connects standards-derived governance objectives to four control layers: governance objectives, design- time constraints, runtime mediation, and assurance feedback, and demonstrates the method in a procurement-agent case study.

2604.05230.tldr: This work provides efficient implementations of the Natural Gradient (NG) optimizer, Self-Scaling BFGS and Broyden optimizers, and addresses the challenge of scaling these quasi-Newton optimizers for batched training, enabling efficient and scalable solutions for large data-driven problems.

2604.05254.tldr: A hybrid deep learning framework for proactive supply chain risk management that jointly models temporal order-flow dynamics via a lightweight Transformer patch encoder and inter-hub relational dependencies through an Edge-Aware Graph Attention Network (E-GAT), optimized via a multi-task learning objective.

2604.05257.tldr: A temporal extension of TabDDPM is proposed, introducing sequence awareness through the use of lightweight temporal adapters and context-aware embedding modules, and demonstrating that diffusion based models provide effective and adaptable solutions for sequential data synthesis when they are equipped for temporal reasoning.

2604.05274.tldr: Only by combining improving evaluator capabilities, adaptive test design, and mutational dynamics do the authors see significant reductions in deception while maintaining alignment fitness (permutation test, $p_{\text{adj}}<0.001$).

2604.05278.tldr: Spec Kit Agents, a multi-agent SDD pipeline that adds phase-level, context-grounding hooks, is presented, a multi-agent SDD pipeline (with PM and developer roles) that adds phase-level, context-grounding hooks.

2604.05279.tldr: This work proposes the first approach to sycophancy reduction via reward decomposition, introducing a multi-component Group Relative Policy Optimisation (GRPO) reward that decomposes the training signal into five terms: pressure resistance, context fidelity, position consistency, agreement suppression, and factual correctness.

2604.05297.tldr: A novel theoretical concept: the stable point, which characterizes the potential convergence of value factorization in general cases is introduced and a novel Multi-Round Value Factorization (MRVF) framework is proposed, which transforms inferior actions into unstable points and drives each iteration toward a stable point with a superior action.

2604.05306.tldr: It is suggested that effective uncertainty in LLMs should be trained as task-matched communication: global confidence for deciding whether to trust a final answer, and local signals for deciding when intervention is needed.

2604.05336.tldr: This work introduces TRACE (Turning Recurrent Agent failures into Capability-targeted training Environments), an end-to-end system for environment-specific agent self-improvement and scales more efficiently than baselines.

2604.05343.tldr: The Anchored Cyclic Generation (ACG) paradigm is proposed, which relies on anchor features from already identified music to guide subsequent generation during the autoregressive process, effectively mitigating error accumulation in autoregressive methods.

2604.05345.tldr: An agentic AI profiler that classifies natural language responses into four levels: Novice, Basic, Advanced, and Expert is proposed that uses a modular layered architecture built on LLaMA v3.1 (8B), with components for text preprocessing, scoring, aggregation, and classification.

2604.05348.tldr: Findings support white-box internal signals grounded in retinal evidence as a practical route to interpretable medical LLM risk triage in diabetic retinopathy decision settings.

2604.05355.tldr: This work proposes Entropy Trend Reward (ETR), a trajectory-aware objective that encourages progressive uncertainty reduction while allowing limited local exploration and consistently achieves a superior accuracy-efficiency tradeoff.

2604.05358.tldr: LatentAudit, a white-box auditor that pools mid-to-late residual-stream activations from an open-weight generator and measures their Mahalanobis distance to the evidence representation, is introduced, position residual-stream geometry as a practical basis for real-time RAG faithfulness monitoring and optional verifiable deployment.

2604.05360.tldr: OGA-AID, a clinician-in-the-loop multi-agent large language model system for multimodal report drafting, demonstrates the feasibility of multimodal agentic systems for structured clinical gait assessment and highlights the complementary relationship between AI-assisted analysis and human clinical judgment in rehabilitation workflows.

2604.05364.tldr: TFRBench establishes a new standard for interpretable, reasoning-based evaluation in time-series forecasting, and proposes a systematic multi-agent framework that utilizes an iterative verification loop to synthesize numerically grounded reasoning traces.

2604.05366.tldr: 3DTurboQuant develops a dimension-dependent criterion that predicts which parameters can be quantized and at what bit-width before running any experiment, deriving norm-separation bounds connecting quantization MSE to rendering PSNR per scene, and an entry-grouping strategy extending rotation-based quantization to 2-dimensional hash grid features.

2604.05368.tldr: This work built a system that uses a semi-structured AI interviewer to elicit personal experiences on policy topics and an interactive visualization that displays predicted policy support alongside those voiced experiences that increased perceived legitimacy, trust in outcomes, and understanding of others' perspectives.

2604.05371.tldr: Study of the feasibility of using a large language model (LLM) as a semantic judge to assess the reliability of power line segmentation results produced by drone-mounted models suggests that, when carefully constrained, an LLM can serve as a reliable semantic judge for monitoring segmentation quality in safety-critical aerial inspection tasks.

2604.05383.tldr: The feasibility of leveraging cross-domain demonstrating examples to boost the LLMs'reasoning performance is demonstrated, and an effective retrieval method, called domain-invariant neurons-based retrieval, called DIN-Retrieval is proposed.

2604.05394.tldr: Assistive Impulse Neural Control is proposed, a framework that reformulates external assistance in impulse space rather than force space to ensure numerical stability in physics-based character animation, and enables robust tracking of highly agile, dynamically infeasible maneuvers that were previously intractable for physics-based methods.

2604.05396.tldr: This study validates the feasibility of leveraging cross-domain knowledge transfer to improve cross-domain ICL performance, motivating the community to explore designing more effective retrieval approaches for this novel direction.

2604.05400.tldr: HYVE offers a practical approximation to an effectively unbounded context window for prompts dominated by large machine-data payloads and is evaluated on diverse real-world workloads spanning knowledge QA, chart generation, anomaly detection, and multi-step network troubleshooting.

2402.09664.tldr: It is shown that LLMs, depending on their size and training strategy, can reason about some dynamic aspects of code, but their performance drops for code with higher complexity, non-trivial logical and arithmetic operators, non-primitive types, and API calls.

2406.14514.tldr: This work considers a Stackelberg game in a dynamic crime scenario where the attacker changes location over time while the defenders attempt to interdict the attacker on his escape route and develops an approximation algorithm on the layered networks to find near-optimal strategy for defenders.

2407.14971.tldr: Sim-CLIP is introduced, an unsupervised adversarial fine-tuning framework that enhances the robustness of the CLIP vision encoder while preserving overall semantic representations and is established as an effective and scalable solution for robust vision-language representation learning.

2409.19894.tldr: This work proposes TransAGENT, a novel multi-agent system that eliminates the errors during LLM-based code translation via fine-grained execution alignment between source and target code and outperforms the latest UniTrans in translation accuracy.

2410.10238.tldr: ForgeryGPT is proposed, a novel framework that advances the IFDL task by capturing high-order forensics knowledge correlations of forged images from diverse linguistic feature spaces, while enabling explainable generation and interactive dialogue through a newly customized Large Language Model (LLM) architecture.

2411.05961.tldr: This paper introduces an edge-cloud collaborative VQA system, called LLaVA-AlignedVQ, which features a novel Aligned Vector Quantization algorithm (AlignedVQ) that efficiently compress intermediate features without compromising accuracy to support partitioned execution.

2501.14183.tldr: This work introduces k-dominant frequency hashing (k-DFH), which utilizes the ranked dominant frequencies in the frequency domain as a hash value to efficiently group variate tokens exhibiting similar periodic behaviors and reduces the token usage by omitting redundant variate tokens during training.

2504.05995.tldr: This work systematize and extend the earlier NativQA framework to multimodality by adding image, audio, and video support, enabling scalable construction of culturally and regionally aligned QA datasets in native languages.

2505.16932.tldr: Polar Express is introduced, a new method for computing the polar decomposition that uses only matrix-matrix multiplications and minimizes error in a worst-case sense, allowing Polar Express to converge as rapidly as possible both in the early iterations and asymptotically.

2506.18601.tldr: This work introduces BulletGen, an approach that takes advantage of generative models to correct errors and complete missing information in a Gaussian-based dynamic scene representation, achieving state-of-the-art results on both novel-view synthesis, and 2D/3D tracking tasks.

2506.21872.tldr: A comprehensive examination of Continual Reinforcement Learning, focusing on its core concepts, challenges, and methodologies is provided, and a new taxonomy of CRL methods is proposed, categorizing them into four types from the perspective of knowledge storage and/or transfer.

2507.10610.tldr: This work systematically study how pop-up-based environmental injection attacks alter the attention behavior of GUI agents and uncover a layer-wise attention divergence pattern between correct and incorrect outputs, and proposes LaSM, a layer-wise attention modulation that selectively amplifies attention and MLP modules in critical layers.

2507.20546.tldr: This work focuses on developing a hallucination detection framework for black-box generators, motivated by the observation that hallucinations, once introduced, tend to persist, and sample future contexts to provide valuable clues for hallucination detection.

2509.17766.tldr: This work proposes a training-free prompt engineering method, the State-Update Multi-turn Dialogue Strategy, which utilizes state reconstruction and history remind Mechanisms to effectively manage dialogue history.

2603.21357.tldr: AgentHER is introduced, a framework that recovers this lost training signal by adapting the Hindsight Experience Replay principle to natural-language agent trajectories for offline data augmentation through a four-stage pipeline that converts discarded failures into high-quality SFT, DPO, and ShareGPT training data.

2603.23448.tldr: A fresh look is taken at the problem and curate a code review dataset for AI agents to work with and observes that the agent reviews often consider different aspects from the human reviews -- indicating the potential for human-agent collaboration for code review that could be deployed in future software teams.

2603.29328.tldr: This paper proposes SABLE, a Semantics-Aware Backdoor for LEarning in federated settings, which constructs natural, content-consistent triggers and optimizes an aggregation-aware malicious objective with feature separation and parameter regularization to keep attacker updates close to benign ones.

2603.29493.tldr: MemFactory is presented, the first unified, highly modular training and inference framework specifically designed for memory-augmented agents, and abstracts the memory lifecycle into atomic, plug-and-play components, enabling researchers to seamlessly construct custom memory agents via a "Lego-like" architecture.

2603.29875.tldr: It is argued that entity-based decomposition yields a more distilled representation of original information, and additionally serves to reduce noise in the indexing, and generation process, and serves to reduce noise in the indexing, and generation process.

2604.02623.tldr: eTAMP is introduced, the first attack to achieve cross-session, cross-site compromise without requiring direct memory access and Frustration Exploitation is discovered: agents under environmental stress become dramatically more susceptible, with ASR increasing up to 8 times when agents struggle with dropped clicks or garbled text.

2604.04037.tldr: This work argues that neural networks represent far more features than dimensions through superposition, and connects representation geometry to distillation limits and provides a practical tool for predicting distillation performance from SAE measurements alone.

2604.04074.tldr: This case suggests that AI is most useful in peer review not as a final decision-maker, but as a tool for gathering evidence and helping reviewers produce more evidence-grounded assessments.

2604.04192.tldr: The results reveal that current models fall short on the core challenges of professional design: spatial reasoning over complex layouts, faithful vector code generation, fine-grained typographic perception, and temporal decomposition of animations remain largely unsolved.

2604.04328.tldr: This work provides a self-contained account that re-centers general-agent evaluation on a robust tournament-theoretic foundation, moving from unstable rankings toward stable, set-valued equilibria.

2604.04403.tldr: Molecular language model with masked Diffusion with mAsking is proposed, a novel multimodal framework that replaces the conventional AR backbone with a discrete Large Language Diffusion Model and mathematically reformulate Molecular Structure Preference Optimization specifically for the masked diffusion.

2604.04917.tldr: Vero, a family of fully open VLMs that matches or exceeds existing open-weight models across diverse visual reasoning tasks, is introduced, a family of fully open VLMs that matches or exceeds existing open-weight models across diverse visual reasoning tasks.

2604.05416.tldr: This paper proposes MAPFZ, a novel MAPF variant on graphs with non-unit integer costs that preserves a finite state space while offering improved realism over classical MAPF, and develops CBS-NIC, an enhanced Conflict-Based Search framework incorporating time-interval-based conflict detection and an improved Safe Interval Path Planning algorithm.

2604.05424.tldr: A novel reasoning framework that draws inspiration from human parallel thinking and reflective processes, PRISM-MCTS integrates a Process Reward Model (PRM) with a dynamic shared memory, capturing both Heuristics and Fallacies and scales inference by reasoning judiciously rather than exhaustively.

2604.05432.tldr: Back-Reveal is presented, a data exfiltration attack that embeds semantic triggers into fine-tuned LLM agents that exposes a critical vulnerability in LLM agents with tool access and highlights the need for defenses against exfiltration-oriented backdoors.

2604.05435.tldr: An automated framework for large-scale auditing of discharge summaries using locally deployed Large Language Models (LLMs) is proposed, which demonstrates the feasibility of scalable, automated clinical auditing and provides a foundation for systematic quality improvement in electronic health record documentation.

2604.05436.tldr: Extensive experiments show that HUG3D significantly outperforms both single-human and existing multi-human methods, producing physically plausible, high-fidelity 3D reconstructions of interacting people from a single image.

2604.05440.tldr: An open-source, governance-aware agentic AI platform for unified security operations, LanG uniquely satisfies multiple industrial capabilities all in one open-source tool, while enforcing selected AI governance policies.

2604.05445.tldr: VL-MDR (Vision-Language Multi-Dimensional Reward), a framework that dynamically decomposes evaluation into granular, interpretable dimensions, consistently outperforms existing open-source reward models on benchmarks like VL-RewardBench.

2604.05458.tldr: MA-IDS is proposed, a Multi-Agent Intrusion Detection System that combines Large Language Models (LLMs) with Retrieval Augmented Generation with Retrieval Augmented Generation for reasoning-driven intrusion detection, demonstrating that retrieval-augmented reasoning offers a principled path toward explainable, self-improving intrusion detection for IoT networks.

2604.05460.tldr: A score-whitening method that equalizes local Fisher information and restores stable inference at the optimal sample-complexity scale is introduced that provides a principled framework for uncertainty quantification in LLM evaluation and more broadly for inference on low-rank structures from pairwise data.

2604.05465.tldr: An adaptive engineering framework that optimizes serverless performance through event-driven architecture and probabilistic modeling is presented, which proposes a dual-strategy mechanism that dynamically adjusts idle durations and employs an intelligent request waiting strategy based on slot survival predictions.

2604.05468.tldr: A novel encoder-decoder framework OntoTKGE is proposed that leverages the ontological knowledge from the ontology-view KG to guide the TKG extrapolation model's learning process through the effective integration of the ontological and temporal knowledge, thereby enhancing entity embeddings.

2604.05481.tldr: A large-scale empirical study on 500 SWE-bench Verified instances using GPT-5-mini, evaluating 61 configurations that vary file-level, element-level, and line-level context shows that more context does not consistently improve repair performance.

2604.05482.tldr: A novel diagnostic paradigm is proposed that reframes the task as a synergistic process of signal localization and spectral detection and identifies pneumothorax by detecting statistically significant outlier eigenvalues that represent a non-random pathological signal.

2604.05483.tldr: A novel algorithm, named as GMRL-BD, designed to identify the untrustworthy boundaries (in terms of topics) of a given LLM, with black-box access to the LLM and under specific query constraints is introduced.

2604.05485.tldr: This work defines five dimensions of agent auditability, i.e., action recoverability, lifecycle coverage, policy checkability, responsibility attribution, and evidence integrity, and identifies three mechanism classes whose temporal information-and-intervention constraints explain why, in practice, no single approach suffices.

2604.05497.tldr: Findings indicate that dMLLMs tend to generate premature final answers without sufficiently grounding on visual inputs, and proposes Position and Step Penalty (PSP) and Visual Reasoning Guidance (VRG) to address these limitations.

2604.05514.tldr: This work proposes OmniDiagram, a unified framework that incorporates diverse diagram code languages and task definitions and introduces a novel visual feedback strategy named Visual Interrogation Verifies All (\textsc{Viva}), to address the challenge of aligning code logic with visual fidelity in Reinforcement Learning (RL).

2604.05517.tldr: Analysis of the proposed UniCreative model reveals an emergent meta-cognitive ability: the model learns to autonomously differentiate between tasks requiring rigorous planning and those favoring direct generation, validating the effectiveness of the direct alignment approach.

2604.05520.tldr: A two-stage framework that eliminates the need for 3D data at inference time is proposed that improves RMSE by up to 7.8% over image-only baselines, while operating on the same input feature space and requiring no 3D data during inference, offering a practical alternative for scalable radio environment modelling.

2604.05526.tldr: A novel singing style conversion system that advances fine-grained style conversion and control within in-domain settings that achieves the best naturalness performance among all submissions while maintaining competitive results in speaker similarity and technique control, despite using significantly less extra singing data than other top-performing systems.

2604.05530.tldr: An exhaustive inventory of the invariant landscape classes for pseudo-Boolean functions of dimensions 1, 2, and 3, including non-injective cases is provided, finding that non-injective functions yield far more invariant landscape classes than injective ones.

2604.05533.tldr: Echo is proposed, a transfer-oriented memory framework that enables agents to derive actionable knowledge from prior interactions rather than treating memory as a passive repository of static records, and leverages In-Context Analogy Learning to retrieve relevant experiences and adapt them to unseen tasks through contextual examples.

2604.05535.tldr: SignalCLAW, a framework that uses large language models LLMs as evolutionary skill generators to synthesize and refine interpretable control skills for adaptive TSC, is presented, making policies human-inspectable and self-documenting.

2604.05536.tldr: This work represents text as a trajectory in a high-dimensional embedding space generated by transformer-based language models, and quantifies scale-dependent fluctuations along the token sequence using an embedding-step signal, suggesting that semantic information is integrated in a scale-free, self-similar manner across linguistic scales.

2604.05537.tldr: It is shown that CNF formulas of treewidth $k$ can be represented by TDDs of FPT size, which is known to be impossible for OBDD.

2604.05539.tldr: A neurosymbolic approach to validating offer documents in regulated public institutions, which employs a language model to extract information and then aggregate with an LTN (Logic Tensor Network) to make an auditable decision.

2604.05547.tldr: Experiments show that COSMO-Agent training substantially improves small open-source LLMs for constraint-driven design, exceeding large open-source and strong closed-source models in feasibility, efficiency, and stability.

2604.05551.tldr: This study shows that when models only have a few denoising steps, inaccurate self-conditioning induces a substantial approximation gap; this mistake compounds across denoising steps and ultimately dominate the sample quality, and proposes a novel training framework that handles errors during learning by perturbing the self-conditioning signal to match inference noise, improving robustness to prior estimation errors.

2604.05587.tldr: This work presents ResearchEVO, an end-to-end framework that computationally instantiates this discover-then-explain paradigm, and is the first system to cover this full pipeline end to end.

2604.05589.tldr: An empirical study of OpenClaw a widely used single-agent assistant, examines OpenClaw's technical design via static code analysis and applies differential forensic analysis to identify recoverable traces across stages of the agent interaction loop, and proposes an agent artifact taxonomy that captures recurring investigative patterns.

2604.05591.tldr: A modular platform that brings together six AI services, automatic speech recognition via OpenAI Whisper, multilingual translation through Meta NLLB, speech synthesis using AWS Polly, emotion classification with RoBERTa, dialogue summarisation via flan t5 base samsum, and International Sign rendering through Google MediaPipe is introduced.

2604.05593.tldr: It is found that both humans and LLM judges assign higher trust to information labeled as human-authored than to the same content labeled as AI-generated, which indicates that the source label is a salient heuristic cue for both humans and LLMs.

2604.05605.tldr: INTERACT (Inclusive Networking for Translation and Embodied Real-Time Augmented Communication Tool), an AI-driven XR platform that integrates real-time speech-to-text conversion, International Sign Language (ISL) rendering through 3D avatars, multilingual translation, and emotion recognition within an immersive virtual environment, is presented.

2604.05616.tldr: StyleMixDG (Style-Mixing for Domain Generalization), a lightweight, model-agnostic augmentation recipe that requires no architectural modifications or additional losses, is derived, confirming that the empirically identified design principles translate into practical gains.

2604.05620.tldr: This work proposes a novel Semantic-Topological Graph Reasoning (STGR) framework for language-guided pulmonary screening, which elegantly synergizes the reasoning capabilities of large language models with the zero-shot delineation of vision foundation models (MedSAM), and introduces a Text-to-Vision Intent Distillation module to extract precise diagnostic guidance.

2604.05631.tldr: It is argued that the field requires an epistemological transition comparable to the cognitive revolution: not an abandonment of behavioral evidence, but a recognition that behavioral evidence alone is insufficient for the construct claims the field wishes to make.

2604.05634.tldr: PECKER introduces a saliency mask to prioritize updates to parameters that contribute most to forgetting the targeted data, thereby reducing unnecessary gradient computation and shortening overall training time without sacrificing unlearning efficacy.

2604.05649.tldr: RATNet is an analogical reasoning mechanism that matches image-derived posterior knowledge to a learned prior knowledge base and transfers relative knowledge to guide diagnosis, improving generalization and resistance to bias, making it a practical foundation for intelligent gastrointestinal diagnosis, especially in resource-limited settings.

2604.05652.tldr: The Domain-Decomposed and Shifted Physics-Informed Neural Network (DDS-PINN), a framework designed to resolve such multiscale interactions with minimal supervision, is proposed, demonstrating strong potential for the super-resolution of complex turbulent flows from sparse experimental measurements.

2604.05655.tldr: This work characterizes large language models'chain-of-thought generation as a structured trajectory through representation space that traverses functionally ordered, step-specific subspaces that become increasingly separable with layer depth and introduces trajectory-based steering, an inference-time intervention framework that enables reasoning correction and length control based on derived ideal trajectories.

2604.05656.tldr: SnapFlow is a plug-and-play self-distillation method that compresses multi-step denoising into a single forward pass (1-NFE) for flow-matching VLAs, orthogonal to layer-distillation and token-pruning approaches, enabling compositional speedups.

2604.05674.tldr: The proposed ASTRAL (Architecture-Centric Security Threat Risk Assessment using LLMs), an architecture-centric security assessment technique implemented in a prototype tool powered by multimodal LLMs, suggests that it can support more informed cyber risk management decisions.

2604.05681.tldr: LudoBench provides a lightweight and interpretable framework for benchmarking LLM strategic reasoning under uncertainty in Ludo, a stochastic multi-agent board game whose dice mechanics, piece capture, safe-square navigation, and home-path progression introduce meaningful planning complexity.

2604.05688.tldr: Attention Editing is presented, a practical framework for converting already-trained large language models (LLMs) with new attention architectures without re-pretraining from scratch, demonstrating that large-scale attention conversion is both feasible and robust.

2604.05689.tldr: Consistent-Recurrent Feature Flow Transformer is presented, a unified coarse-to-fine framework based on feature flow learning for robust cross-modal image registration that consistently outperforms state-of-the-art registration methods in both accuracy and robustness.

2604.05711.tldr: SemLink is proposed, a novel automated test oracle for semantic hyperlink verification that bridges the gap between traditional syntactic checkers and expensive generative AI, offering a robust and efficient solution for automated web quality assurance.

2604.05716.tldr: Through analyses of output trajectories and ablation studies, it is found that generative verifier in the reinvention phase plays a critical role in sustaining models'reasoning strength, helping to avoid the ``thought collapse''phenomenon.

2604.05719.tldr: This paper presents the first Systematization of Knowledge (SoK) focusing on the architectural design and comprehensive empirical evaluation of current LLM-based AutoPT frameworks and provides researchers with a structured taxonomy to understand existing LLM-based AutoPT frameworks and a large-scale empirical benchmark.

2604.05755.tldr: A benchmark called CAKE is presented, which consists of 188 expert-validated questions covering four cognitive levels of Bloom's revised taxonomy -- recall, analyze, design, and implement -- and five cloud-native topics, suggesting that the evaluation format fundamentally shapes how the authors measure architectural knowledge in LLMs.

2604.05777.tldr: Using reinforcement learning simulations, it is shown how minimal social learning can indirectly transmit higher-level representations, and how cultural transmission can arise from simple, non-mentalizing processes exploiting asocial learning mechanisms.

2604.05779.tldr: Using the knowledge score, a fine-grained, instance-level knowledge score is reliably estimated via multi-sampled inference, and evaluation metrics for uncertainty are proposed, showing that accurate discrimination between known and unknown instances consistently improves performance.

2604.05826.tldr: It is argued that AI systems should be recognized, as least to some extent, as artifacts capable of exercising a form of agency, thereby enabling them to engage in relationships of trust or distrust with humans and the implications for regulators tasked with overseeing AI systems.

2604.05830.tldr: The experimental results indicate that these demographics-agnostic training techniques markedly reduce demographic bias, leading to a more equitable performance profile across different speaker groups.

2604.05839.tldr: These findings indicate that automated, VLM-based critique of frontend code generation leads to significantly higher quality solutions than can be achieved through a single LLM inference pass, and highlight the importance of iterative refinement for the complex visual outputs associated with web development.

2604.05848.tldr: This work examines how to evaluate learner representations based on whether they retain separation between learners under a shared comparison rule, and introduces distinctiveness, a representation-level measure that evaluates how each learner differs from others in the cohort using pairwise distances.

2604.05854.tldr: An open-source framework that enables large language model (LLM) agents to autonomously conduct deep learning experiments around the clock and introduces three key innovations, including a monitoring paradigm that incurs zero LLM API costs during model training by relying solely on process-level checks and log file reads.

2604.05856.tldr: Experiments demonstrate that the proposed Hybrid QUBO significantly outperforms both greedy Taylor pruning and traditional L1-based QUBO, with TT Refinement providing further consistent gains at appropriate combinatorial scales, highlighting the potential of hybrid combinatorial formulations for robust, scalable, and interpretable neural network compression.

2604.05859.tldr: LLMP-UCB, a bandit algorithm that derives uncertainty estimates from LLMs via repeated inference, is introduced, providing a principled deployment framework for cost-effective, uncertainty-aware decision systems with broad applicability across AI use cases in financial services.

2604.05865.tldr: JTON (JSON Tabular Object Notation), a strict JSON superset whose main idea, Zen Grid, factors column headers into a single row and encodes values with semicolons, preserving JSON's type system while cutting redundancy.

2604.05872.tldr: This paper introduces Swiss-Bench 003 (SBP-003), extending the HAAS (Helvetic AI Assessment Score) from six to eight dimensions by adding D7 (Self-Graded Reliability Proxy) and D8 (Adversarial Security) and provides conceptual mapping tables relating benchmark dimensions to FINMA model validation requirements, nDSG data protection obligations, and OWASP LLM risk categories.

2604.05875.tldr: By combining the strengths of the LLM with the SLM, a novel framework JCQL is proposed, which can make these two tasks enhance each other in an iterative manner and surpasses all baselines for both KBC and KBQA tasks.

2604.05877.tldr: This work replicates the ante-mortem image with the 3D model to perform the morphological comparison, providing an automatic, objective and quantitative score of the morphological correspondence, easily to interpret and analyze by visualizing superimposed images.
